Connecting real accounts also needs a paid plan: free applications can only create items on the Sandbox (Pluggy Bank) and MeuPluggy connectors, and any other connector returns `400 CLIENT_PLAN_REAL_CONNECTORS_NOT_ALLOWED` — see [Error Codes](/reference/error-codes#creating-and-updating-an-item).

## Deleting your Pluggy account

Source: https://docs.pluggy.ai/en/docs/get-started/delete-account.md

## Deleting a developer account

Closing a **developer account** — the login you use on
[dashboard.pluggy.ai](https://dashboard.pluggy.ai) — is not a self-service action
in the Dashboard. To close one, write to us:

- **E-mail**: [support@pluggy.ai](mailto:support@pluggy.ai), or
  [sales@pluggy.ai](mailto:sales@pluggy.ai) if your team is on a paid plan and
  the account is tied to a contract.
- Tell us the **e-mail address of the account** to close, from that same address
  where possible, so we can confirm it is yours.

Other contact channels, and which one fits which situation, are in
[Contact and support](/docs/get-started/contact).

<Callout variant="warning" title="This is not the same as deleting an Item">
Deleting an **Item** removes one end user's bank connection and its data, and you
can do that yourself at any time with
[`DELETE /items/{id}`](/reference/items-delete) — see
[Item lifecycle](/docs/connections/item-lifecycle#data-retention-and-automatic-cleanup).
Deleting your **account** is about your own Pluggy login and the applications it
owns.
</Callout>

## What closing the account removes

- **Every application you own**, together with its client credentials — the API
  keys of those applications stop working, so anything still calling the API with
  them will start failing.
- **The teams where you are the only member, or the last remaining `OWNER`.** If
  a team should survive you, promote another member to `OWNER` **before** asking
  for the deletion, or the team is removed with your account.
- **The account itself.** The e-mail address is released, so you can sign up
  again later with the same address if you need to.

<Callout variant="info" title="Delete the Items you no longer need first">
If you have live connections you want gone, delete those Items explicitly while
you still have working API keys. It is the clean way to end the connections, and
it revokes the Open Finance consent where one applies.
</Callout>

## Data protection requests (LGPD)

A request to access, correct or erase **personal data** is a different process
from closing an account, and it goes to Pluggy's Data Protection Officer:

- **E-mail**: [dpo@pluggy.ai](mailto:dpo@pluggy.ai)
- Requests for correction, deletion or a copy of the data held about you may take
  **up to 15 days**, as stated in
  [Pluggy's privacy policy](https://www.pluggy.ai/legal).

If you are an **end user** — you connected your own bank account through a
product built on Pluggy — ask that product to delete your data: it owns the
connection, and Pluggy processes the data on its behalf. For accounts connected
through [Meu Pluggy](https://meu.pluggy.ai), send these data protection requests
to [dpo@pluggy.ai](mailto:dpo@pluggy.ai) from your Meu Pluggy account's e-mail;
any other problem with the account goes to
[meu-suporte@pluggy.ai](mailto:meu-suporte@pluggy.ai).

## One application, or one per client?

Source: https://docs.pluggy.ai/en/docs/get-started/multi-tenant-applications.md

If your product serves many companies — an accounting platform, an ERP, a SaaS
where each customer is a separate organisation — you can give **each tenant its
own production application**, with its own `client_id` and `client_secret`.

You can also run everything through a single application. Both are supported,
and the choice is yours.

## What separate applications give you

Each application is its own boundary, so one per tenant means:

- **Separate credentials.** A leaked or rotated `client_secret` affects one
  tenant, not all of them.
- **Its own [webhook](/docs/developer-tools/webhooks-ref) URL**, so events
  arrive already attributed to a tenant instead of needing to be routed after
  the fact.
- **Its own [Pluggy Connect customization](/docs/connect-widget/customization)** —
  company name and logo are set on the application in the Dashboard, so the
  account holder sees the right brand while authorizing their bank.
- **A clean audit boundary.** Items created under one application are reachable
  only with that application's credentials — `GET /items/{id}` with the wrong
  application's key does not return another tenant's Item.

<Callout variant="warning" title="More applications do not mean more request budget">
[Rate limits](/docs/reference/rate-limits) are counted **per endpoint, per IP,
per minute** — explicitly *not* per account and not per API key. Every server
behind the same egress IP shares one budget no matter how many applications it
authenticates as. If you are splitting into one application per tenant to get
more throughput, it will not work; spread the traffic across egress IPs, or
across time, instead.
</Callout>

## What it does not decide

Two things are commercial rather than technical, and they are not the same
question as how you lay out applications:

- Whether the connections included in your plan are counted per application or
  across the account.
- What a second, third or fiftieth production application implies for your
  contract.

Those belong with Sales — [sales@pluggy.ai](mailto:sales@pluggy.ai) or the
WhatsApp on the [pricing page](https://www.pluggy.ai/precos). Ask before you
build the layout around an assumption.

## The consent stays with the account holder

Whichever layout you choose, the person who authorizes the bank connection is
the **account holder**, in their own bank's environment. That does not change
because your customer is a company that serves other companies: an accounting
firm cannot authorize on behalf of the company whose data it reads. Each
account holder connects their own institution through Pluggy Connect, and the
[Item](/docs/connections/item-lifecycle) that results belongs to the application
the connection was created under.

## Slack Integration

Source: https://docs.pluggy.ai/en/docs/integrations/slack.md

## Overview

Pluggy runs a **hosted, public Slack bot** that answers questions from Pluggy's live documentation right inside Slack. Add it to your workspace and your team can ask about the API, look things up, and get answers with doc links — without leaving Slack and without building anything.

Just like the [MCP server](/docs/developer-tools/mcp), the bot is **hosted by Pluggy**: there's no Slack app to create, no OAuth scopes to configure, no request URLs, and no environment variables. You add it and use it.

## Add the bot to your workspace

Click **Add to Slack** and approve the install for your workspace (you'll need workspace-admin permission to install apps):

<a href="https://v2.docs.pluggy.ai/api/slack/install">
  <img
    alt="Add to Slack"
    height="40"
    width="139"
    src="https://platform.slack-edge.com/img/add_to_slack.png"
  />
</a>

That's the whole setup. Once installed, invite the bot to any channel where you want to use it.

## Use it

- **Mention it** in a channel it's in:

  ```
  @Pluggy Docs how do I create a connect token and open the Connect Widget?
  ```

- **Direct-message it** a question — no command needed:

  ```
  What scopes does the Connect Widget need?
  ```

The bot replies with a concise answer grounded in Pluggy's documentation, with links to the relevant guides.

## What it can access (today)

For now the bot answers from Pluggy's **public documentation** only — the same content served at [v2.docs.pluggy.ai](https://v2.docs.pluggy.ai): guides, API reference, changelog, recipes, and curated Q&A. It does **not** access your Pluggy account, applications, or data.

<Callout variant="info" title="Coming soon — sign in for team answers">
  Like the MCP server, the bot will optionally let you **sign in with your Pluggy dashboard account** and keep a session, so it can answer questions scoped to **your team** — your applications, items, and usage. Until you sign in — and today, in v0 — it stays on the **public docs**.
</Callout>

## Privacy

The bot only reads the messages that mention it or that you DM it, uses them to search the documentation, and replies. It doesn't store your Slack data.

## Troubleshooting

- **The bot doesn't reply** — make sure it's been **invited to the channel** (mentions only work where the bot is a member), or try a direct message.
- **"Add to Slack" didn't install** — you need **workspace-admin** permission to add apps; ask your Slack admin to run the install.
- **Answers look off or outdated** — the bot answers from the live public docs; if something's wrong in the docs themselves, let the Pluggy team know.

## Security overview

Source: https://docs.pluggy.ai/en/docs/security/overview.md

Your Pluggy credentials reach your users' financial data. Pluggy runs the connections to the
institutions, keeps each Item's credentials and data, and delivers your webhooks, signed once you
turn signing on. Your
side of the integration is yours to secure: your credentials, the tokens you hand to the front end,
your webhook endpoint, your team, and the data you copy into your own systems.

Each section below is a summary with a link to the page that has the details. The
[checklist](#checklist) at the end sums them up.

## Credentials stay on your server

Your application's client secret, and the API keys your server creates with it, have full access
to the Pluggy API. Keep them in a secrets manager or a server environment variable, reuse each API
key until it expires, and use separate applications for development and production. Generating a
new client secret stops the old one immediately but does not revoke API keys created before it.

Details: [Credentials and API keys](/docs/security/credentials). Recipe:
[Rotate your client secret](/recipes/rotate-your-client-secret).

## The front end gets a Connect Token, never an API key

Your backend creates a Connect Token for a signed-in user, and the front end opens Pluggy Connect
with it. It lasts 30 minutes, reaches only the Items created with it, and cannot read product data.
Set `clientUserId` to an opaque identifier, and leave `includeSandbox` off in production.

Details: [Connect Tokens](/docs/security/connect-tokens). Recipe:
[Issue Connect Tokens from your backend](/recipes/issue-connect-tokens-from-your-backend).

## Verify every webhook notification

Your webhook endpoint is public, so treat every request as untrusted until it passes your checks.
Combine the layers: an HTTPS endpoint, a secret in the webhook's `headers`, and the
**`X-Pluggy-Signature`** HMAC signature, which proves that Pluggy sent the notification and that its
body was not altered. Then check `clientId` and read the current state with your API key instead of
trusting the payload. Source-IP filtering is an extra layer, never the only one.

Details: [Webhook security](/docs/developer-tools/webhook-security). Recipe:
[Authenticate webhook notifications with a header secret](/recipes/authenticate-webhook-notifications-with-a-header-secret).

## Only the right people manage your applications

A team has three roles. Owners and Admins generate client secrets and manage webhooks; only Owners
disable or delete applications and manage the webhook signing secret. Keep `OWNER` and `ADMIN` for
the people who need them, and rotate secrets when someone who could see them leaves.

Details: [Team access](/docs/security/team-access).

## Your users' data and consent

Let Pluggy Connect collect bank credentials, so they never pass through your servers. Let users
disconnect, and delete the Item when they do: that wipes its credentials, revokes the consent and
deletes its data. Remove your own copy on `item/deleted`, and store only what your product uses.

Details: [Data protection](/docs/security/data-protection).

## Report a vulnerability

If you find a security vulnerability in Pluggy, write to
[security@pluggy.ai](mailto:security@pluggy.ai). The same contact is published in our
[`security.txt`](https://docs.pluggy.ai/.well-known/security.txt).

## Checklist

| Area | Check |
| --- | --- |
| Credentials | The client secret lives only in a secrets manager or server environment variable. |
| Credentials | No client secret or API key is in front-end code, mobile apps, repositories or logs. |
| Credentials | Your server reuses each API key until it expires. |
| Credentials | Development and production use separate applications. |
| Credentials | You know how to generate a new client secret, where to deploy it, and how to disable the application if an API key leaks. |
| Front end | The front end receives only Connect Tokens, created by your backend for an authenticated user. |
| Front end | `clientUserId` is an opaque identifier, not personal data. |
| Front end | `includeSandbox` is off in production. |
| Webhooks | Your endpoint verifies `X-Pluggy-Signature` over the raw body, with a 5-minute tolerance. |
| Webhooks | Webhooks created with `POST /webhooks` carry a secret header that your endpoint requires. |
| Webhooks | Your endpoint ignores notifications for other `clientId`s, answers `2xx` quickly and reads the data with your API key. |
| Access | Only the people who need it are `OWNER` or `ADMIN` of your team. |
| Access | Members who leave are removed, and the secrets they could see are rotated. |
| Data | Users can disconnect, and disconnecting deletes the Item. |
| Data | You remove your copy of the data on `item/deleted`. |

## Credentials and API keys

Source: https://docs.pluggy.ai/en/docs/security/credentials.md

Every application in the [Dashboard](https://dashboard.pluggy.ai) has its own credentials, and
together they reach every Item of that application. This page covers where each one may live and
what to do when one is exposed.

## The three credentials

| Credential | What it is | Where it may live |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Client ID | Identifies the application. Shown in the Dashboard at any time. | Your server. It is not a secret on its own, but it is only useful together with the client secret. |
| Client secret | Proves you own the application. Shown **once**, when it is generated. | Your server only: a secrets manager or an environment variable. |
| API key | Created by your server with [`POST /auth`](/reference/auth-create) from the client ID and secret. It has **full access** to every endpoint of the Pluggy API. | Your server only, in memory. |

The front end never gets any of them. It gets a [Connect Token](/docs/security/connect-tokens),
which your backend creates for one user.

## Store the client secret like a password

- Keep it in a secrets manager or an environment variable of your server. Never commit it, never
  log it, and never put it in front-end code, a mobile app, a ticket or a chat message.
- Read it from one place. Then a rotation is one update and a redeploy, not a search through
  repositories.
- New client secrets start with `pluggy_sk_` and carry a checksum, so secret scanners can recognize
  one that ends up in a repository. See
  [Client secret format](/docs/authentication#client-secret-format).
- The secret cannot be viewed again after the dialog that shows it is closed: not in the Dashboard
  and not through the API. If you lose it, generate a new one.

## Use the API key from your server only

- Create an API key with `POST /auth` and reuse it until it expires, instead of calling `POST /auth`
  on every request. The [lifetime](/docs/authentication#create-an-api-key) and the
  [rate limit of `POST /auth`](/reference/rate-limits) are on their own pages. When a request
  answers `401` because the key expired, create a new one.
- The Node.js SDK (`pluggy-sdk`) creates the API key and reuses it for you.
- Never send an API key to a browser or a mobile app, and never log it: anyone who holds it has the
  same access as your server until it expires.

## Separate development, production and tenants

- **One application per environment.** Each application has its own client ID and client secret,
  so a development secret that leaks does not reach production data. See
  [Environments and production](/docs/get-started/faq#environments-and-production).
- **One application per tenant**, if you serve several companies: Items are reachable only with the
  credentials of the application they were created under, so a leaked or rotated secret affects one
  tenant. See [One application, or one per client?](/docs/get-started/multi-tenant-applications).
- **Going to production rotates the secret.** When an application is moved to production, its
  secret is rotated and the Dashboard asks an Owner or Admin to generate a new one. Plan the deploy
  of the new secret for that moment.

## Rotate the client secret

Generate a new secret in the Dashboard, on the application's page. Only a team's Owners and Admins
can do it (see [Team access](/docs/security/team-access)).

- The current secret stops working **immediately**: from that moment `POST /auth` with it fails.
  Any service that needs a new API key fails until it has the new secret, so know which services
  use it before you click.
- The new secret is shown **once**. Store it in your secrets manager before closing the dialog.
- Generating a new secret **does not revoke the API keys created before it**. They keep working
  until they expire.

Recipe, with a script that checks the new secret before you redeploy:
[Rotate your client secret](/recipes/rotate-your-client-secret).

## If a credential leaks

**A client secret.** Generate a new one right away, deploy it, and remove the old value from
wherever it was exposed (repository history, logs, tickets). Then check what was done with the
application while the secret was valid.

**An API key**, or a secret that was used to create API keys you do not control. A new client
secret does not stop those keys. To cut them off before they expire, an Owner can **disable the
application** in the Dashboard: while it is disabled, the API rejects its API keys and Connect
Tokens, and `POST /auth` answers `401` with `CLIENT_DISABLED`. Everything that uses the application
stops with it, your own services included.

<Callout variant="warning" title="Re-enabling restores unexpired API keys">
Disabling does not revoke an API key: it blocks the application. When you enable it again, every API
key that has not expired yet works again, including a leaked one. Generate a new client secret
while the application is disabled, and enable it only after the API keys created before the
rotation have expired.
</Callout>

## Does not protect against

- A secret stolen from a server you control: rotation limits how long it stays useful, but your
  secrets manager and server access are yours to protect.
- An API key in front-end code: rotating the secret does not revoke it. Keep keys on the server.

Next: [Connect Tokens](/docs/security/connect-tokens).

## Connect Tokens

Source: https://docs.pluggy.ai/en/docs/security/connect-tokens.md

Browsers and mobile apps are not a safe place for a secret: anything shipped to them can be read.
So the front end never gets your client secret or an API key. It gets a **Connect Token**, a
short-lived credential that your backend creates for one user and one connection.

## Issue it from your backend, for a signed-in user

1. Your server creates an API key with `POST /auth` (see [Credentials](/docs/security/credentials)).
2. Your server creates a Connect Token with [`POST /connect_token`](/reference/connect-token-create),
   from an endpoint that only your **signed-in users** can call.
3. The front end receives the Connect Token and opens [Pluggy Connect](/docs/connect-widget/introduction)
   with it.

Protect that endpoint with your own authentication. Anyone who can call it can open Pluggy Connect
on your behalf and connect accounts to your application.

Recipe: [Issue Connect Tokens from your backend](/recipes/issue-connect-tokens-from-your-backend).
Details: [Pluggy Connect authentication](/docs/connect-widget/authentication).

## What a Connect Token can reach

- The Items created with that token, through [`GET /items/{id}`](/reference/items-retrieve), and a
  reduced view of their accounts, through `GET /accounts?itemId=`.
- Nothing created with another Connect Token.
- No product data: transactions, investments, identity and every other product require an API key.
  A Connect Token gets `403 Forbidden`.

So a Connect Token that leaks exposes at most the connections made with it, and only until it
expires.

## How long it lasts

A Connect Token is valid for **30 minutes**. Create a new one for each connection instead of
caching it or sharing it between users.

While an application is [disabled](/docs/security/credentials#if-a-credential-leaks), its Connect
Tokens are rejected too.

## Options that matter for security

Options go inside `options` in the body of `POST /connect_token`; a property sent at the root is
ignored. See [Configuring a Connect Token](/docs/authentication#configuring-a-connect-token).

| Option | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `clientUserId` | Set it to an opaque identifier from your system, not an e-mail address or a CPF. It is stored on the Item and sent in every `item/*` webhook payload. |
| `itemId` (at the root) | Scopes the token to one existing Item, to update it. Check that the Item belongs to the signed-in user before you create the token. See [Updating an Item](/docs/connect-widget/updating-item). |
| `webhookUrl` | Must be a public HTTPS URL. It does not send custom headers, so protect it with the [signature](/docs/developer-tools/webhook-security#4-verify-the-signature), or use a webhook created with `POST /webhooks` instead. |
| `oauthRedirectUri` | Must be HTTPS or a deep link into your app. See [OAuth Support Guide](/docs/connect-widget/oauth-support). |

On the widget, leave `includeSandbox` off in production: Sandbox connectors are for testing. See
[Environments and Configurations](/docs/connect-widget/environments).

## Does not protect against

- An endpoint that issues Connect Tokens to anyone: the token is only as safe as the authentication
  in front of it.
- Updating the wrong user's Item: the API scopes the token to the `itemId` you pass, but only your
  backend knows which user owns which Item.

Next: [Webhook security](/docs/developer-tools/webhook-security).

## Team access

Source: https://docs.pluggy.ai/en/docs/security/team-access.md

Your team's members manage the applications that hold your credentials, so who is on the team,
and with which role, is part of your security. A team has three roles: `OWNER`, `ADMIN` and
`MEMBER`.

## What each role can do

| Action in the Dashboard | `OWNER` | `ADMIN` | `MEMBER` |
| --- | :-: | :-: | :-: |
| See applications and list their webhooks | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Create applications and edit their name, description and origins | Yes | Yes | No |
| Generate a new client secret | Yes | Yes | No |
| Create, update and delete webhooks | Yes | Yes | No |
| Set a webhook's custom headers | Yes | No | No |
| Generate, regenerate or remove the webhook signing secret | Yes | No | No |
| Enable or disable an application | Yes | No | No |
| Delete an application | Yes | No | No |
| Change the Pluggy Connect customization | Yes | Yes | No |
| Invite members, change their roles and remove them | Yes | Yes, except `OWNER`s | No |
| Make someone an `OWNER` | Yes | No | No |
| See billing and submit the due diligence | Yes | Yes | No |
| Delete the team | Yes | No | No |

An `ADMIN` can invite and manage `ADMIN`s and `MEMBER`s, but cannot invite or promote anyone to
`OWNER`, and cannot change the role of an existing `OWNER` or remove one.

These rules apply to the Dashboard. Anyone who holds the application's client secret or an API key
can do everything the API allows, whatever their role: see [Credentials](/docs/security/credentials).

## Least privilege

- **Give `OWNER` to few people.** An `OWNER` can disable and delete applications, manage the
  webhook signing secret and hand out `OWNER` to others.
- **Give `ADMIN` to the people who operate the integration.** An `ADMIN` can generate a new client
  secret, and with it, read the new secret.
- **Everyone else is a `MEMBER`.** A `MEMBER` can follow the integration in the Dashboard without
  changing applications, secrets or webhooks.
- **Keep at least two `OWNER`s** if your team should survive one person leaving. A team whose last
  `OWNER` closes their Pluggy account is deleted with it; see
  [Deleting your Pluggy account](/docs/get-started/delete-account).

## When someone leaves

1. **Remove them from the team** in the Dashboard. To remove an `OWNER`, another `OWNER` has to do
   it.
2. **Rotate the client secret** of every application whose secret they could have seen: an
   `OWNER` or `ADMIN` who generated one, or anyone who could read your secrets manager. Removing a
   member does not change the application's credentials. See
   [Rotate the client secret](/docs/security/credentials#rotate-the-client-secret).
3. **Regenerate the webhook signing secret** and the secret in your webhooks' headers if they had
   access to them. See [Rotating the secret](/docs/developer-tools/webhook-security#rotating-the-secret).

API keys created before a rotation keep working until they expire. If you need to cut them off
sooner, see [If a credential leaks](/docs/security/credentials#if-a-credential-leaks).

## Does not protect against

- A secret copied out of the Dashboard: roles control who can generate or change it, not where it
  goes afterwards.
- Access through the API: it is governed by your credentials, not by team roles.

Next: [Data protection](/docs/security/data-protection).

## Data protection

Source: https://docs.pluggy.ai/en/docs/security/data-protection.md

Your users' financial data reaches your systems through Pluggy. What Pluggy stores for each Item,
and when it deletes it, is documented below with links to the details. What you copy into your own
systems is yours to protect.

## Keep bank credentials out of your servers

With [Pluggy Connect](/docs/connect-widget/introduction), your users type their bank credentials
in the widget, which sends them to Pluggy with the Connect Token: they never pass through your
backend. Prefer it to building your own credential form.

If you do collect credentials in your own interface and create Items through the API, encrypt the
`parameters` with your application's RSA public key, which you get from Pluggy: only Pluggy can
decrypt them. Recipe: [Encrypt parameters](/recipes/encrypt-parameters).

## The account holder gives the consent

The person who authorizes a connection is the account holder, in their own institution's
environment. A company that serves other companies cannot authorize on their behalf. See
[The consent stays with the account holder](/docs/get-started/multi-tenant-applications#the-consent-stays-with-the-account-holder).

When a consent expires, or the user revokes it, the Item's data endpoints return empty data. Only
the user can renew it, by connecting again. See
[Consents and expiration](/docs/connections/consents#consent-expiration--revocation).

## Let users disconnect

Give your users a way to disconnect an account at any time, and delete the Item when they do, with
[`DELETE /items/{id}`](/reference/items-delete) from your backend. Deleting an Item:

- wipes its stored credentials,
- revokes the Open Finance consent, where one applies, and expires OAuth authorizations,
- permanently deletes its data (accounts, transactions and the rest).

After that, the Item and its products answer `404`. See
[Consent management](/docs/integration-checklist/consent-management) and the
[Deleting your Data](/recipes/deleting-your-data) recipe.

## React when Pluggy deletes an Item

Pluggy also deletes Items on its own, for example Sandbox Items not used for 30 days, and every Item
of a connector 30 days after the connector is deprecated. Each deletion emits the `item/deleted`
webhook. Subscribe to it and remove your copy of the data when it arrives. See
[Data retention and automatic cleanup](/docs/connections/item-lifecycle#data-retention-and-automatic-cleanup).

## Store only what you use

- **Keep what your product needs**, and delete it when the user leaves or disconnects. Your API key
  can read the data again while the Item exists.
- **Use opaque identifiers.** Set `clientUserId` to an internal id, not an e-mail address or a CPF:
  it is stored on the Item and sent in webhook payloads.
- **Keep personal data out of logs and error reports.** Financial data and identity fields
  (names, CPF or CNPJ, account numbers) do not belong in a log line, an analytics event or a support
  ticket.
- **Restrict who can read it** in your own systems, the same way you restrict who can read your
  client secret.

## Data protection requests

A request from an **end user** to access, correct or erase their data goes to the product they
connected through, which owns the connection: that is you. Delete their Items to remove the data
Pluggy holds for them.

Requests about your **own** personal data as a Pluggy customer go to Pluggy's Data Protection
Officer. See [Data protection requests (LGPD)](/docs/get-started/delete-account#data-protection-requests-lgpd).

## Does not protect against

- Copies you made: deleting an Item removes Pluggy's data, not what your systems stored. That part
  is up to you.

Next: [Security overview checklist](/docs/security/overview#checklist).

## Sandbox

Source: https://docs.pluggy.ai/en/docs/guides/sandbox.md

Using our production environment you can access `Live` and `Sandbox` connectors. For testing purposes, you can experiment with your integration using our **Sandbox connector** (which represents our `Sandbox` environment). This will let you see how the transactions update over time and test all the possible valid connections and erroneous flows. Sandbox transactions are refreshed weekly and may also change daily, so the environment is not static.

<Callout variant="warning" title="Warning">
All the sandbox items that are not updated for more than **30 days** will be deleted without any possibility to get them back in the future.
</Callout>

**You will find different flows:**

1. Basic flow (we also include a special device authorization flow)
2. Basic flow Business
3. MFA 1-step
4. MFA 2-step
5. Joint accounts (Bradesco Conta Conjunta flow)
6. QR Login flow
7. Open Finance flow

**For a successful flow, the credentials are:**

- **Correct password**: `password-ok`
- **Correct MFA Token**: `123456`

Each test user name below maps to a specific execution status. See [Item lifecycle](/docs/connections/item-lifecycle) for the full description of item and execution statuses.

## Sandbox response structure

The Sandbox (Pluggy Bank connector) returns synthetic data, but with the same field structure as production responses. Below is the field mapping observed in `/accounts` , `/transactions` , `/investments` , and `/loans` for a test item queried.

### Accounts

```json /accounts
// Always returns at least 1 BANK/CHECKING_ACCOUNT and 1 CREDIT/CREDIT_CARD account:
{
    "type": "BANK", "subtype": "CHECKING_ACCOUNT",
    "balance": 21544.6, "currencyCode": "BRL",
    "marketingName": "GOLD Conta Corrente", "taxNumber": "333.333.333-33", "owner": "John Doe",
    "bankData": {
      "transferNumber": "123/0001/12345-0",
      "closingBalance": 21544.6,
      "automaticallyInvestedBalance": 2154.46,
      "hasReservedBalance": true,
      "reservedBalances": [{ "name": "Caixinha Para Férias", "availableAmounts": [{ "amount": 1000.04, "remuneration": { "indexer": "CDI", "rateType": "LINEAR", "preFixedRate": 0.3 } }] }]
    },
    "creditData": null
  }

  {
    "type": "CREDIT", "subtype": "CREDIT_CARD",
    "balance": -503.1,
    "creditData": {
      "level": "BLACK", "brand": "MASTERCARD",
      "balanceCloseDate": "2026-07-23", "balanceDueDate": "2026-07-28",
      "creditLimit": 300000, "availableCreditLimit": 300000,
      "minimumPayment": 100.62, "holderType": "MAIN", "status": "ACTIVE"
    }
  }

// Note that bankData/creditData are mutually exclusive depending on the account's type - the Sandbox even simulates reservedBalances ("piggy banks") inside bankData, which isn't trivial to find documented elsewhere.
```

### Transactions

```json /transactions
// Simple transaction (recurring, no extra metadata) — salary, recurring debits:
  { "description": "SALARIO EMPRESA XYZ LTDA", "amount": 8500, "type": "CREDIT", "category": "Salary", "categoryId": "01010000", "paymentData": null,
  "creditCardMetadata": null }

// Bank slip (boleto) payment — the only record with paymentData populated:
  {
    "description": "Pagamento de boleto", "amount": -100, "type": "DEBIT",
    "category": "Transfer - Bank Slip", "categoryId": "05010000",
    "paymentData": {
      "payer": { "documentNumber": { "type": "CPF", "value": "111.111.111-11" }, "name": "Francisco Souza", "routingNumberISPB": "60701190" },
      "paymentMethod": "BOLETO",
      "receiver": { "documentNumber": { "type": "CNPJ", "value": "PL.UGG.Y12/AB00-42" }, "name": "Pluggy Brasil Instituição de Pagamento LTDA" },
      "boletoMetadata": { "baseAmount": 90, "discountAmount": 0, "interestAmount": 10, "digitableLine": "11190000111001113911100000021110600000000111000" }
    }
  }

// Installment credit card purchase — the only record with creditCardMetadata populated:
  {
    "description": "NETFLIX.COM", "amount": -55.9,
    "creditCardMetadata": { "installmentNumber": 2, "totalInstallments": 6, "totalAmount": -335.4, "payeeMCC": 5812, "billId":
  "3b3341e4-d30c-48d6-bcbe-79a3fe47d704" }
  }

// In other words: the Sandbox simulates bank-slip (boleto) payments and installment card purchases, but the checking account queried here has no Pix, TED, or inter-account transfers — all 17 checking-account transactions are: boleto payment, recurring debits (telecom, electricity, condo fees), salary, and bill payment. On the credit card, all 9 transactions are purchases (subscriptions/gym), with no dispute, refund, or cash-advance examples.
```

### Investments

```json /investments

    "balance": 1359.39, "quantity": 3, "value": 500, "amount": 1500,
    "taxes": 40.61, "taxes2": 100, "amountProfit": 359.39, "amountOriginal": 1000
  }

  // FIXED_INCOME/CDB — fixed-income bond
  {
    "type": "FIXED_INCOME", "subtype": "CDB", "name": "CDR",
    "balance": 2000, "rate": 150, "rateType": "CDI", "fixedAnnualRate": 2.5,
    "dueDate": "2026-07-23T16:16:27.300Z", "issuer": "Banco do Pluggy",
    "institution": { "name": "BANCO BTG PACTUAL S/A", "number": "30306294000145" }
  }

  // ETF/ETF — appears twice: one active, one fully withdrawn
  {
    "type": "ETF", "subtype": "ETF", "name": "ISUS11 STOCK", "code": "ISUS11", "isin": "123456789",
    "quantity": 1, "amount": 2000, "status": "ACTIVE"
  }
  {
    "type": "ETF", "subtype": "ETF", "name": "BOVA11", "code": "BOVA11",
    "quantity": 0, "value": 118.4, "status": "TOTAL_WITHDRAWAL"
  }

  // EQUITY/REAL_ESTATE_FUND — REIT (FII)
  {
    "type": "EQUITY", "subtype": "REAL_ESTATE_FUND", "name": "GGRC11", "code": "GGRC11", "isin": "BRGGRCCTF002",
    "quantity": 1, "amount": 118.4, "issuer": "GGR COVEPI RENDA FDO INV IMOB"
  }

  // No SECURITY/individual-stock example (equity held outside a fund), and nothing explicitly
  // labeled Treasury Direct — the closest analog available is the FIXED_INCOME/CDB above.
```

### Loans

## 1- Basic flows

<Callout variant="info" title="Note">
The basic flow also works for **Business connectors**.
</Callout>

| Execution status | User name | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `SUCCESS` | `user-ok` | Successful connection. |
| `ALREADY_LOGGED_IN` | `user-logged` | The user already has an opened login session (needs to manually log out). |
| `ACCOUNT_LOCKED` | `user-locked` | User account is locked, needs manual action to be unlocked. |
| `UNEXPECTED_ERROR` | `user-error` | Connector had a random error. |
| `SITE_NOT_AVAILABLE` | `user-unavailable` | Provider site was not available. |
| `ACCOUNT_NEEDS_ACTION` | `user-account-need-actions` | Provider is requesting some manual action from the user (ie. accept new terms of use). |
| `ACCOUNT_NEEDS_ACTION` + `providerMessage` | `user-account-need-actions-provider-message` | Provider is requesting some manual action from the user, including instructions to address it in the item error `providerMessage` field. |
| `CONNECTION_ERROR` | `user-connection-error` | There was an internal connection error with the provider (ie. Proxy issue). |
| `INVALID_CREDENTIALS` | anything else | The user/password credentials were invalid. |
| `PARTIAL_SUCCESS` | `user-ok-account-error` | Error recovering account product. |
| `SUCCESS` with warnings | `user-ok-account-warning` | Warning in account product. |
| `ACCOUNT_CREDENTIALS_RESET` | `user-account-credentials-reset` | The user needs to update some of their credentials in the institution. |
| `USER_NOT_SUPPORTED` | `user-not-supported` | The user is not allowed to perform login in the institution through Pluggy. |
| `SUCCESS` with two checking accounts data | `user-ok-two-checking-accounts` | Success, but returns an example of two checking accounts. |

### Enlarge result data

In cases in which it is necessary to test large amounts of transactions in the result, you can use the `user-ok-perf` or `user-ok-perf-XXx` username to recreate this situation. `XX` represents the multiplier for the number of transactions to be retrieved. For example, if you choose 1000 as XX, the resulting username would be `user-ok-perf-1000x`, in order to multiply the result by this number.

The limit of this multiplier is 5000, so if you use a larger number, the multiplier will be just 5000.

### Basic Flow | Authorization Pending status (device authorization flow)

This is a special case that emulates a connector that requires the user to authorize a device. It consists of three possible execution statuses to be returned.

When a user connects for the first time, the expected execution returned will be to confirm the user device shown (i.e. "1234-5678").

So, the first execution (after the user confirms the device on his side) will return `USER_AUTHORIZATION_PENDING` and a message that informs the time that the user must wait until authorization is granted by the institution.

Once this step is completed, there are two possible scenarios:

1. If the user updates the item within the time to be awaited, the execution result will be `USER_AUTHORIZATION_NOT_GRANTED` and a message to remind the time to be awaited until the authorization is granted by the institution (in the Sandbox case, the time is 2 minutes).
2. If the user updates the item after the wait is over, the data of the account will be retrieved successfully and the execution report will be `SUCCESS`.

See the table below for more details:

| Execution status | User name | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `USER_AUTHORIZATION_PENDING` | `user-ok-auth-pending` | This will report a `USER_AUTHORIZATION_PENDING` status, and a message to wait for 2 minutes until the institution grants authorization. Then, you can update the item to retrieve the data after those 2 minutes, or get a not-yet-granted authorization message (please read the next rows). |
| `USER_AUTHORIZATION_NOT_GRANTED` | re-use credentials (update) | If the item is updated before the institution grants authorization, the status reported will be `USER_AUTHORIZATION_NOT_GRANTED` and you will be newly asked to wait for the 2 minutes after the first execution. |
| `SUCCESS` | re-use credentials (update) | If the item is updated once the institution authorization is completed, then the data should be retrieved and the status report will be `SUCCESS`. |

## 3- MFA 1-step

| Scenario | User name | MFA | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Login Ok | `user-ok` | `123456` | Successful connection. |
| `INVALID_CREDENTIALS_MFA` | `user-ok` | ≠ `123456` | The MFA parameter provided was incorrect. |

| Scenario | User name | MFA | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Login Ok | `user-ok` | `123456` | Successful connection. |
| `INVALID_CREDENTIALS_MFA` | `user-ok` | ≠ `123456` | The MFA parameter provided was incorrect. |
| Login Ok (MFA with QR image) | `user-ok-img` | `123456` | Successful connection. |
| `INVALID_CREDENTIALS_MFA` (MFA with QR image) | `user-ok-img` | ≠ `123456` | The MFA parameter provided was incorrect. |
| Login Ok (MFA with options to select) | `user-ok-select` | any | Successful connection. |
| Login OK (with phone selection before MFA) | `user-ok-phone` | `123456` | Successful connection. |
| `INVALID_CREDENTIALS_MFA` (with phone selection before MFA) | `user-ok-phone` | ≠ `123456` | The MFA parameter provided was incorrect. |
| Login Ok (with company selection after MFA) | `user-ok-multi-company` | `123456` | Successful connection. |
| `INVALID_CREDENTIALS_MFA` | `user-ok-multi-company` | ≠ `123456` | The MFA parameter provided was incorrect. |
| `UNEXPECTED_ERROR` | `user-ok-mfa-error` | `123456` | Connector had a random error. |
| `ACCOUNT_LOCKED` | `user-ok-mfa-locked` | `123456` | User account is locked, needs manual action to be unlocked. |
| `SITE_NOT_AVAILABLE` | `user-ok-mfa-unavailable` | `123456` | Provider site was not available. |
| `CONNECTION_ERROR` | `user-ok-mfa-connection-error` | `123456` | There was an internal connection error with the provider (ie. Proxy issue). |
| `ALREADY_LOGGED_IN` | `user-ok-mfa-logged` | `123456` | The user already has an opened login session (needs to manually log out). |
| `ACCOUNT_NEEDS_ACTION` | `user-ok-mfa-account-need-actions` | `123456` | Provider is requesting some manual action from the user (ie. accept new terms of use). |

## 5- Joint Accounts (Bradesco Conta Conjunta flow)

This is a special case that emulates the Bradesco Conta Conjunta flow.

**Below you will find two examples:**

1. Testing in the Pluggy Connect widget
2. Testing via Postman

### 1- Testing in the Pluggy Connect widget

When using the [Pluggy Connect widget](/docs/connect-widget/introduction), the user will be presented to choose first from either a "Single account" or a "Joint account".

- If the user selects **"Single account"**, they will be asked for bank credentials and MFA in the same step as the credentials.
- If the user selects **"Joint account"**, they will be asked only for bank credentials. Then, they will be asked which account they want to connect, and after that, the MFA will be required. If the MFA is correct, the account will connect successfully.

### 2- Testing via Postman

- When testing "single account", the request is the same as sandbox MFA 1-step. The bank credentials and MFA are sent together.
- When testing "joint account", you have to include an MFA 1-step parameter, with the mock value: `000000`.

Note that this is the same as the Connect widget flow. When the user selects the "joint account" flow, the UI is not asking to complete the MFA parameter.

## 6- QR Login flow

This is a case that originally simulates a flow similar to Inter QR. No credentials are necessary. Once started, the item will enter a `WAITING_USER_ACTION` status, and return a QR code for the user to scan.

This flow will simulate a rapidly changing QR code for 10 seconds and then simulate the user reading the QR and advancing the state to a normal login flow.

## 7- Open Finance flow

To connect using our sandbox connection (see [Creating an Open Finance item](/docs/open-finance/creating-item)), you will be required to send a CPF:

| Scenario | CPF |
|---|---|
| Basic flow | 761.092.776-73 |
| Multiple authorization flow - approved | 238.242.640-30 |
| Multiple authorization flow - rejected | 051.177.670-55 |
| Basic flow - with slow authentication | 002.502.737-99 |
| Basic flow - force error getting OF resources | 163.511.711-99 |

This will redirect you to the mock bank login page. Please use the following credentials:

- User: `user-ok`
- Password: `password-ok`

### How does the multiple authorization (múltipla alçada) flow work?

This flow simulates a scenario where, in order to retrieve account data, the item must be approved by another person (typically another company associate). To test this scenario, follow these steps:

1. Create a sandbox item using one of the CPFs listed in the table above. The item will not return accounts immediately. Instead, the `statusDetail` field will indicate that the accounts require authorization.
2. Update that item. Depending on the CPF you provided, the accounts may or may not be returned.

## Testing payments and boletos

Payment initiation and boletos have their own sandbox institutions. For PIX, create the Payment Request with `isSandbox: true`; a sandbox request only accepts sandbox connectors, and a live request only live ones. The consent page of the sandbox bank asks for `user-ok` / `password-ok`. Boletos have no Payment Request: create a boleto connection with the sandbox connector `8` instead.

| Payment type | Connector | Required inputs | How it completes in sandbox | Webhooks |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PIX (immediate) | `600` | Payment intent `parameters.cpf`: `76109277673` | Within seconds of approving the `consentUrl` | `payment_intent/created`, `payment_intent/completed`, `payment_request/updated` |
| Scheduled PIX (Pix Agendado) | `600` | Payment initiation for scheduled payments enabled on your account; payment request with a `schedule`; intent `parameters.cpf`: `76109277673` | At consent time, as a single payment — the scheduled dates are not waited for | `payment_intent/created`, `scheduled_payment/completed` |
| Pix Automático | `600` | CNPJ recipient; intent `parameters.cpf`: `76109277673` and `parameters.name` | A `firstPayment` with no date or dated today runs right after consent, with a later `startDate`; a future `firstPayment` and scheduled payments (D+2 to D+10) run at 09:00 UTC on their date | `payment_intent/created`, `payment_intent/completed`, `payment_request/updated`, `automatic_pix_payment/created`, `automatic_pix_payment/completed` |
| Boleto | `8` | A boleto connection with empty `credentials`; the cents of the `amount` pick the scenario | By itself, one step every 5 minutes | `boleto/updated` |

Scheduled PIX uses your own payment initiation agreement, so payment initiation for scheduled payments must be enabled on your account, also to test it in sandbox. Without it, `POST /payments/intents` returns `403` with `PAYMENT_INITIATION_NOT_ALLOWED` for a payment request with a `schedule`, in sandbox as well. Contact Pluggy support to enable it.

An amount of `404.04` makes the sandbox bank (`600`) reject the payment synchronously — `POST /payments/intents` fails for an immediate or scheduled PIX or a Pix Automático first payment, and the schedule request fails for a Pix Automático charge — so you can test your error handling.

Step-by-step guides:

- PIX (immediate): [Testing payments with Sandbox bank](/docs/payments/overview#testing-payments-with-sandbox-bank)
- Scheduled PIX: [Scheduled Payments — Testing in sandbox](/docs/payments/scheduled-payments#testing-in-sandbox)
- Pix Automático: [Getting Started — Testing in sandbox](/docs/payments/pix-getting-started#10-testing-in-sandbox) and the [scheduler's sandbox timing](/docs/payments/pix-scheduler#testing-in-sandbox)
- Boleto: [Testing with the Sandbox](/docs/boleto/sandbox)

## Dashboard: connectors, test connections and the itemId

Source: https://docs.pluggy.ai/en/docs/guides/dashboard-connectors.md

Three things every integration needs from the [Pluggy Dashboard](https://dashboard.pluggy.ai), with the exact place to click. The same steps work for any connector — a bank, an Open Finance institution, or the **MeuPluggy** connector for personal use (see [Personal use with Meu Pluggy](/docs/guides/meu-pluggy-personal-use)).

## 1. Choose which connectors Pluggy Connect shows

Connector selection is set once for your **team** and applies to every application's Pluggy Connect widget.

1. In the left menu, open **Customization** (under *Financial Data*).
2. Go to the **Connectors** tab.

![Customization page, Connectors tab](/docs/images/dashboard/customization-connectors-tab.png)

3. Pick a mode:
   - **Default to all selected** — every available connector is shown.
   - **Custom selection active** — only the connectors you switch on are shown.
4. Use the search box to find a connector by name (for example `MeuPluggy`, `Itaú`, `Nubank`). Results are grouped by category (*Personal*, *Business*, *Investment*); open a group and choose between its **OF Connectors** and **Direct Connectors** tabs — **MeuPluggy** is a Direct connector (it carries the *Direct* badge). In custom mode, turn the connector's switch on.

![Searching a connector and switching it on](/docs/images/dashboard/customization-connector-search.png)

5. Use **Preview** on the right to open the real widget and check the list your users will see.

<Callout variant="info" title="Keep at least one connector">
Pluggy Connect always needs at least one connector selected. Branding (name, logo, colors, button text) lives in the **General** tab of the same page — see [Customization](/docs/connect-widget/customization).
</Callout>

## 2. Connect an account from the Dashboard

You do not need a frontend to test a connection: every application has a **Demo** page that opens Pluggy Connect for you.

1. Open **Applications** and click the application you want to use (the gear icon opens its settings).
2. Open its **Demo** page and click **Connect Account**.

![Demo page with the Connect Account button](/docs/images/dashboard/demo-connect-account.png)

3. Pick the institution in the widget and finish the connection. The **Sandbox** connector is always listed here (search `Sandbox`), so you can test with the [sandbox credentials](/docs/guides/sandbox) on any plan; the item it creates is called *Pluggy Bank*.

![Pluggy Connect opened from the Dashboard](/docs/images/dashboard/demo-widget.png)

## 3. Find the itemId

Every connection creates an **Item**, and its id — the `itemId` — is what the API reads data with (`GET /accounts?itemId=…`).

1. On the same **Demo** page, the left column **Connected Items** lists the application's items.
2. Click an item: its detail shows the **itemId** with a copy button, plus its accounts, identity and investments.

![Item detail with the itemId copy button](/docs/images/dashboard/demo-item-id.png)

In your own integration the `itemId` also arrives in the widget's `onSuccess` callback and in every `item/*` webhook — store it when the connection is created. See [Item](/docs/connections/item).

## 4. Client ID and Client Secret

1. Open **Applications**. Each application shows its **Client ID**, which you can copy at any time.
2. The **Client Secret** is shown **only once**, when it is generated: when you create the application, or when you click **Generate new secret** on the application's page. Copy it into your secrets manager right away — the dialog only closes after you confirm you stored it.
3. Exchange both for an API key with `POST /auth` (see [Authentication](/docs/authentication)).

<Callout variant="warning" title="The secret cannot be viewed again">
After that dialog is closed, the Client Secret is not available anywhere — not in the Dashboard and not through the API. If you lose it, click **Generate new secret** on the application's page. The previous secret stops working immediately, so update every integration that uses it.
</Callout>

Only team **Owners** and **Admins** can generate a new secret. When an application is moved to production, its secret is rotated and the Dashboard shows a notice asking an Owner or Admin to generate a new one.

## Common questions

- **"The connector I want is not in the widget."** Check the **Connectors** tab: in custom mode only switched-on connectors appear.
- **"I want real (production) data."** Companies request it with **Unlock real data** on the application (it leads to Sales and due diligence). For **personal use**, choose that option and you are pointed to [Meu Pluggy](/docs/guides/meu-pluggy-personal-use), which is free.

## Personal use: read your own data with Meu Pluggy

Source: https://docs.pluggy.ai/en/docs/guides/meu-pluggy-personal-use.md

If you are an individual who wants to read **your own** bank accounts with code — a personal finance script, a spreadsheet, an app only you use — the path is **Meu Pluggy** plus the **MeuPluggy connector**. It is free, needs no due diligence and does not expire with the trial. It is for personal use only (up to 5 connections, no commercial use).

Companies building a product for their users follow the regular integration instead ([Quick start](/docs/quickstart)) and talk to [Sales](/docs/get-started/contact).

The official guide from Meu Pluggy is at [meu.pluggy.ai/api-guide](https://meu.pluggy.ai/api-guide). This page shows the same four steps with the Pluggy Dashboard screens.

## Step 1 — Connect your banks in Meu Pluggy

Sign up at [meu.pluggy.ai](https://meu.pluggy.ai) and connect your banks there. This is where each bank is authorized (CPF, the bank's app, approval). **Each bank is authorized separately**, and a bank you add later needs its own authorization.

## Step 2 — Add the MeuPluggy connector in the Dashboard

1. Sign in to the [Pluggy Dashboard](https://dashboard.pluggy.ai) **with the same account** you use in Meu Pluggy.
2. If you use a custom connector selection, make sure **MeuPluggy** is switched on: **Customization → Connectors**, search `MeuPluggy` and open the **Direct Connectors** tab of the *Personal* group ([how](/docs/guides/dashboard-connectors#1-choose-which-connectors-pluggy-connect-shows)).
3. Open **Applications → your application → Demo** and click **Connect Account**.
4. In the widget, choose **MeuPluggy** — not your bank, and not the Sandbox — and sign in with your Meu Pluggy account.

![Choosing the MeuPluggy connector in Pluggy Connect](/docs/images/dashboard/meupluggy-connector.png)

Each bank you connected in Meu Pluggy becomes an **item** in this application. These items mirror the Meu Pluggy connection: they reflect every update automatically (Meu Pluggy refreshes every 24 hours), they cannot be updated manually, and they send webhooks like any item.

<Callout variant="warning" title="The most common mistake">
If the Dashboard asks for your CPF and a bank approval again, you picked the bank's own connector instead of **MeuPluggy**. Go back and choose MeuPluggy.
</Callout>

## Step 3 — Copy the itemId and your credentials

- **itemId:** on the same **Demo** page, click the item in **Connected Items** and copy its id ([how](/docs/guides/dashboard-connectors#3-find-the-itemid)). Keep it — `GET /v2/items` is not available for Meu Pluggy accounts.
- **Client ID / Client Secret:** the Client ID is in **Applications**, on your application's row. The Client Secret is shown only once, when it is generated — if you didn't store it, generate a new one on the application's page ([how](/docs/guides/dashboard-connectors#4-client-id-and-client-secret)).

## Step 4 — Read your data

```bash
# 1. Exchange your credentials for an API key
curl -X POST https://api.pluggy.ai/auth \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"clientId": "<client id>", "clientSecret": "<client secret>"}'
# → { "apiKey": "..." }

# 2. List the accounts of one connection
curl "https://api.pluggy.ai/accounts?itemId=<item id>" \
  -H "X-API-KEY: <api key>"

# 3. Transactions of one account (its id comes from step 2)
curl "https://api.pluggy.ai/transactions?accountId=<account id>" \
  -H "X-API-KEY: <api key>"
```

The SDKs ([Node, Python and more](/docs/developer-tools/server-sdks)) make the same calls.

## The authorization expires after one year

When you sign in to Meu Pluggy in Step 2, you authorize your application to read the connections you have there. That authorization is what the MeuPluggy items read through, and it **lasts one year** from the moment you grant it. Each bank connection inside Meu Pluggy keeps its own consent with the bank; this one is separate and sits on top of them.

You can see when it ends on the item itself: [GET /items/\{id\}](/reference/items-retrieve) returns it as `consentExpiresAt`.

### What happens when it expires

- **Reads stop.** Accounts, transactions and the other lists of that item come back empty.
- **The next update fails with a login error.** The item moves to `LOGIN_ERROR` with the code `USER_AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRED`, and the `item/error` webhook fires. If you listen to webhooks, that is your signal.

Until that next update runs, the item can still show its last status — `UPDATED`, with no error — while the reads come back empty. Check `consentExpiresAt`: an empty read with a past date means the authorization lapsed, not that your bank connections stopped syncing.

### How to renew it

Repeat Step 2: open **Applications → your application → Demo**, click **Connect Account**, choose **MeuPluggy** and sign in with your Meu Pluggy account. Granting it starts a new one-year period.

An update triggered by the API or by the automatic sync cannot renew it, because nobody is there to sign in: it ends in `USER_AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRED` as above.

<Callout variant="warning" title="Do not assume the same itemId">
After authorizing again, check which item your data is on before you continue reading. If you store transactions on your side, reconcile them by their own ids rather than assuming the item kept its id.
</Callout>

Deleting your Meu Pluggy account ends the authorization immediately.

## Testing without real data

To try the flow without your own accounts, use the **Sandbox** connector with its [test credentials](/docs/guides/sandbox). Your Meu Pluggy connection is real data, never a sandbox.

## Questions

For a problem with your account or one of your connections, write to [meu-suporte@pluggy.ai](mailto:meu-suporte@pluggy.ai) from your Meu Pluggy account's e-mail. Questions about personal use go to the same address.

## Introduction

Source: https://docs.pluggy.ai/en/docs/connect-widget/introduction.md

## What is Pluggy Connect?

Pluggy Connect is a drop-in widget we offer to help you quickly get started with Pluggy. Your users will use it to connect their accounts, within your app, directly to the Pluggy API.

The Connect Widget is Pluggy's plug & play frontend solution that allows users to connect their financial accounts on a step-by-step flow, so you will only need to worry about interacting with their data instead of worrying about painful login flows.

Throughout the connection process, the widget handles:

- Credential validation
- Multi-factor authentication (MFA)
- Error management

## How it Works

The typical integration follows these key steps:

1. **Backend Token Setup**: First, you'll need to set up an endpoint on your backend that obtains and provides a **Connect Token**. This token grants Pluggy Connect authorization to access the Pluggy API on behalf of your application. This process must be done on your backend, since the endpoint requires authentication using your application's `CLIENT_ID` and `CLIENT_SECRET`.

2. **Frontend Integration**: With your Connect Token endpoint deployed, you are ready to integrate Pluggy Connect in your client-side application. There are fully working frontend examples that you can clone and start using right away to launch the Pluggy Connect interface, by replacing the Connect Token endpoint URL with your own.

3. **User Connection**: When your user clicks on "Connect my account", a Connect Token is obtained and the Connect Widget instantiates with this token and opens up a modal for the user to input their credentials.

4. **Data Retrieval**: Once the widget finishes, it emits an `onSuccess` event with the `id` of the newly created **Item**. This Item ID is needed for any future action you want to do with the connected banking data.

<Video src="https://pluggy.ai/showcase/pluggy-connect.mp4" />

## Platform Support

Pluggy Connect is an easy-to-integrate and quick-to-setup tool that works across all browsers and platforms, including:

- Web (React, Next.js, Plain JavaScript)
- iOS
- Android
- React Native
- Flutter
- Mobile Webviews

## Event Callbacks

The widget supports several callbacks to improve the user experience, such as redirecting users to a success page or showing error messages. You can pass the widget a function to execute when an event happens:

- **onSuccess**: Triggered when the connection is successful. Receives an object containing the item data (e.g., `onSuccess={({ item }) => console.log(item.id)}`).
- **onError**: Triggered when an error occurs. Receives error information and can access the item data if available (e.g., `onError={({ message, data: { item } }) => showErrorPage(message)}`).
- **onClose**: Triggered when the user closes the widget modal.
- **onOpen**: Triggered when the widget is opened.
- **onEvent**: Handles specific user interaction events such as `LOGIN_SUCCESS`, `LOGIN_MFA_SUCCESS`, `LOGIN_STEP_COMPLETED`, and `ITEM_RESPONSE`.

## MFA Support

Pluggy Connect handles multi-factor authentication flows automatically. The first time linking an MFA connection, the user receives an extra parameter in the credentials list (a one-use parameter). If you use the Pluggy Connect widget, you won't need to go into further details of the flow -- Pluggy has already covered it all for you.

## Getting Started

To start using Pluggy Connect, you will need:

1. A Pluggy account with `CLIENT_ID` and `CLIENT_SECRET` (available from the [Dashboard](https://dashboard.pluggy.ai))
2. A backend endpoint that generates Connect Tokens
3. A frontend integration using one of the available SDKs

Check the following sections for more details on [Authentication](/docs/connect-widget/authentication), [Environments and Configurations](/docs/connect-widget/environments), [Updating an Item](/docs/connect-widget/updating-item), [Customization](/docs/connect-widget/customization), and [OAuth Support](/docs/connect-widget/oauth-support).

## Authentication

Source: https://docs.pluggy.ai/en/docs/connect-widget/authentication.md

## Overview

When connecting to Pluggy from a client-side application (i.e. the Connect Widget), we require the use of a **Connect Token**. The Connect Token access is limited to only the generated Item resource data (`GET /items/:id`), and a reduced access to the data of the recovered Accounts (`GET /accounts?itemId`).

A newly created Connect Token can't be used to access information that has been created previously with a different Connect Token.

## Connect Token

A Connect Token is a limited-access token that:

- **Expires 30 minutes** after creation
- Is meant to be used by **frontend applications** (Web or Mobile) to authenticate with Pluggy
- Is specially useful for end-users to connect their accounts through the Pluggy Connect widget
- Has visibility only for the connections that were created using this token

## Authentication Flow

Both API Keys and Connect Tokens can be recovered using the `CLIENT_ID` and `CLIENT_SECRET` provided in the [Dashboard](https://dashboard.pluggy.ai).

![Pluggy Connect authentication flow](/docs/images/connect-flow-diagram.jpg)

The authentication process works as follows:

### 1. Backend Authentication

First, authenticate with the Pluggy API using your `CLIENT_ID` and `CLIENT_SECRET` to create an API Key:

```bash
curl --request POST \
  --url https://api.pluggy.ai/auth \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
    "clientId": "YOUR_CLIENT_ID",
    "clientSecret": "YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET"
  }'
```

### 2. Create a Connect Token

Set up an endpoint on your backend that obtains and provides a Connect Token, which grants Pluggy Connect authorization to access the Pluggy API on behalf of your application:

```bash
curl --request POST \
  --url https://api.pluggy.ai/connect_token \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --header 'X-API-KEY: YOUR_API_KEY' \
  --data '{
    "options": {
      "clientUserId": "your-user-id",
      "webhookUrl": "https://www.myapi.com/notifications"
    }
  }'
```

When creating a Connect Token you can provide some `ItemOptions` that will be passed down to all items created using the same token:

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `clientUserId` | An identifier for the user in your application, useful for traceability |
| `webhookUrl` | URL where Pluggy will send webhook notifications |
| `oauthRedirectUri` | URI to redirect users after OAuth process |
| `avoidDuplicates` | Whether to avoid creating duplicate items |

### 3. Frontend Widget Integration

Use the Connect Token in your frontend application to initialize the Pluggy Connect widget:

```javascript
import PluggyConnect from 'pluggy-connect-sdk';

const pluggyConnect = new PluggyConnect({
  connectToken: 'your-connect-token',
  onSuccess: (itemData) => {
    console.log('Connection successful!', itemData);
  },
  onError: (error) => {
    console.error('Connection error:', error);
  },
});

pluggyConnect.init();
```

Or with React:

```jsx
import { PluggyConnect } from 'react-pluggy-connect';

function App() {
  return (
    <PluggyConnect
      connectToken="your-connect-token"
      onSuccess={({ item }) => console.log(item.id)}
      onError={({ message }) => console.error(message)}
    />
  );
}
```

## Security Warning

<Callout variant="warning" title="Important">
Do not store `clientId` and `clientSecret` in the frontend. If this information is visible in your page's code, an attacker can steal all of your user's banking data.
</Callout>

You need to create a backend endpoint that generates a Connect Token for every user that visits your page. This Connect Token has restricted permissions and duration for security reasons.

The proper architecture is:

1. **Backend** generates the Connect Token using `CLIENT_ID` and `CLIENT_SECRET` (kept secure on the server)
2. **Frontend** receives only the limited-scope Connect Token
3. **Frontend** uses the Connect Token with the Pluggy Connect Widget

## Environments and Configurations

Source: https://docs.pluggy.ai/en/docs/connect-widget/environments.md

Get your web application quickly and seamlessly integrated with our platform by using our drop-in Connect Widget!

## Environments

The Connect Widget runs on a single **Production** environment, available at:

```
https://connect.pluggy.ai
```

Using the production environment you can access both `Live` and `Sandbox` connectors — there is no separate sandbox URL.

### Sandbox testing

For testing purposes, you can experiment with your integration using our **Pluggy Bank** Sandbox connectors. Pluggy Bank's transactions are refreshed weekly and may also change daily, so the environment is not static. It lets you test all the login flows and scenarios you would encounter when using any of the available Live connectors.

To display Sandbox connectors in the Connector selection step, set the `includeSandbox` property to `true` (not intended for production use). It is an option of the **widget**, passed to `new PluggyConnect(...)` — `POST /connect_token` has no such field. Integrating without the widget, list the sandbox connectors with `GET /connectors?sandbox=true`:

```javascript
const pluggyConnect = new PluggyConnect({
  connectToken: 'your-connect-token',
  includeSandbox: true,
  onSuccess: (itemData) => {
    console.log('Success!', itemData);
  },
});
```

#### Pluggy Bank test credentials

For a successful connection with the Pluggy Bank connector, use:

| Field                       | Value          |
| :-------------------------- | :------------- |
| User                        | `user-ok`      |
| Password                    | `password-ok`  |
| MFA token (when requested)  | `123456`       |

Any other username will result in an `INVALID_CREDENTIALS` error. For the full list of test users covering error scenarios (locked account, site not available, MFA flows, Open Finance, and more), check the [Sandbox guide](/docs/guides/sandbox).

## Available configurations

**Note:** all parameters are optional, except for the `connectToken`.

| Property | Description | Type |
| :------- | :---------- | :--- |
| `connectToken` | Your Pluggy Connect token, which will be used to access the API. | `string` |
| `includeSandbox` | Whether to display Sandbox connectors in the Connector selection step (not intended for production use). | `boolean` |
| `allowConnectInBackground` | If `true`, Connect can be minimized by the user to continue the connection with the component hidden. | `boolean` |
| `allowFullscreen` | If set to `false`, Connect won't be displayed as fullscreen on small/mobile screens; it will be displayed as a modal instead. Defaults to `true`. | `boolean` |
| `updateItem` | Item ID to update. If specified, the widget will directly display the credentials form of the Item to be updated. | `string` |
| `selectedConnectorId` | If specified, and the Connector is available, after accepting terms the widget will navigate directly to this Connector's login form, skipping the connector selection step. | `number` |
| `connectorTypes` | List of Connector Types. If defined, only Connectors of the specified connector types (`PERSONAL_BANK`, `BUSINESS_BANK`, etc.) will be listed. Useful for cases of different flows for PF or PJ users. | `ConnectorType[]` |
| `connectorIds` | List of Connector IDs. If defined, only Connectors with the specified connector IDs will be listed. | `number[]` |
| `countries` | List of country codes (ISO-3166-1 alpha-2 format). If defined, only Connectors of the specified countries will be listed. | `CountryCode[]` |
| `products` | If defined, only the products specified in this array will be executed in the Item creation (in order to be executed, you should have them enabled in your team subscription). **Important**: product types must be specified in uppercase letters (`ACCOUNTS`, `CREDIT_CARDS`, `TRANSACTIONS`, etc.). | `ProductType[]` |
| `language` | Language ISO string used to display the widget. If not specified, or if the selected language is not supported, the default language `'pt'` will be used. | `string` |
| `theme` | Theme to use for displaying the UI. Can be `'light'` or `'dark'`. Defaults to `'light'`. | `'light' \| 'dark'` |
| `openFinanceParameters` | Object with CPF and CNPJ for Open Finance connectors only; the form will be pre-filled with these values. Contains optional `cpf` and `cnpj` string fields. | `{ cpf?: string; cnpj?: string }` |
| `forceOauthInBrowser` | If set to `true`, OAuth URLs will always open in the system browser instead of a webview. This helps avoid webview-related issues. This prop takes precedence over the API config value. | `boolean` |
| `forceAskForCredentials` | If set to `true`, the widget will always prompt for credentials when updating an Item, even if the system would normally attempt to update automatically. | `boolean` |
| `onSuccess` | Function to execute when an Item has been created/updated successfully. | `(data: { item: Item }) => void \| Promise<void>` |
| `onError` | Function to execute on a general error loading the widget, or when an Item creation/update status has not been successful. To validate which error happened, check `item.executionStatus`. | `(error: { message: string; data?: { item: Item } }) => void \| Promise<void>` |
| `onOpen` | Function to execute when the widget modal has been opened. | `() => void \| Promise<void>` |
| `onClose` | Function to execute when the widget modal has been closed. | `() => void \| Promise<void>` |
| `onHide` | Function to execute when the widget modal has been hidden. It will only be called if the `allowConnectInBackground` prop is set to `true`. | `() => void \| Promise<void>` |
| `onEvent` | Function to execute to handle custom user interaction events. See [onEvent](#onevent) below for more info. | **Since v2.0.0:**<br />`(payload: ConnectEventPayload) => void \| Promise<void>`<br />**Until v1.x:**<br />`(event: string, metadata: { timestamp: number }) => void` |

## onEvent

Use this callback to handle specific user interaction events.

The `event` property inside the `payload` of `onEvent` is the current event triggered. The available events that can be handled through this method are:

| Event name               | Description                                                                                                                                                               |
| :----------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `'SUBMITTED_CONSENT'`    | User has confirmed terms & privacy consent on the first Welcome screen.                                                                                                   |
| `'SELECTED_INSTITUTION'` | User has selected an institution to connect to.                                                                                                                           |
| `'SUBMITTED_LOGIN'`      | User has submitted credentials to create the connection Item.                                                                                                             |
| `'SUBMITTED_MFA'`        | User has submitted an extra parameter that has been requested by the institution to connect.                                                                              |
| `'LOGIN_SUCCESS'`        | User has submitted credentials to create the connection Item **successfully**.                                                                                            |
| `'LOGIN_MFA_SUCCESS'`    | User has submitted an extra parameter that has been requested by the institution to connect **successfully**.                                                             |
| `'LOGIN_STEP_COMPLETED'` | Successful completion of the login. User effectively logged in to the institution.                                                                                        |
| `'ITEM_RESPONSE'`        | Called every time the Item object is retrieved from the Pluggy API, either when just created, updated, or each time it's retrieved to poll its connection/execution status. |

The `payload` object has a `timestamp` property, and some events include extra data:

- `'SELECTED_INSTITUTION'` includes the `connector` property, which is the connector selected by the user.
- `'LOGIN_SUCCESS'`, `'LOGIN_MFA_SUCCESS'`, `'LOGIN_STEP_COMPLETED'` and `'ITEM_RESPONSE'` include the `item` property, which is the Item data related to the current connection.

<Callout variant="info" title="v2.0.0 signature change">
Since widget version 2.0.0, `onEvent` receives a single payload object: `(payload: ConnectEventPayload) => void`.
In versions 1.x, it received two arguments: `(event: string, metadata: { timestamp: number }) => void`.
</Callout>

## Webhooks and callbacks

After a user makes a connection with the Pluggy Connect Widget, there are two ways to get the recently created Item ID.

### Connect Widget callbacks

In the frontend of your application (website, application, etc.), when you're using the Connect Widget, you get access to [callbacks](#available-configurations). This way, you can pass the widget a function to execute when an event happens (for example, an account connected successfully or with an error). What's important for you to know here is that callbacks are used to improve the user experience, like redirecting users to a success page or showing an error message.

```jsx
<PluggyConnect
  ...
  onSuccess={({ item }) => console.log(item.id)}
  onError={({ message, data: { item } }) => showErrorPage(message)}
/>
```

This approach is great for handling frontend logic, but it is inconsistent by nature: you cannot rely on it for your business logic or database integrity. For example, a user can close the application before the connection finishes successfully, and you will never realize that the connection finished. To be consistent, use webhooks.

<Callout variant="info" title="onSuccess won't always be called!">
Some connectors have authorization flows that require the user to authorize Pluggy as a trusted device, and that approval is not immediate.
In this scenario, you will receive an `onError` with the status `USER_AUTHORIZATION_PENDING`, and the SUCCESS event will be communicated via webhooks.
</Callout>

### Webhooks

A webhook (also known as a web callback) is a simple method that makes it easy for an app or system to provide real-time information whenever an event happens — that is, it is a way to passively receive data between two systems through an `HTTP POST`.

Webhooks will send your API / backend a notification when events related to connections happen. For example, you can get notified when an Item is created or updated (read more in the [Webhooks reference](/docs/developer-tools/webhooks-ref)).

You'll need to create an endpoint to listen to Pluggy's webhook events, and then create a webhook pointing to that endpoint. More details can be found in the [Webhooks reference](/docs/developer-tools/webhooks-ref), but what's important to understand here is that webhooks are the way to get the Item ID of a connection for you to work on. Even though you can also retrieve the Item ID with callbacks in the frontend, handling business logic with them is a bad practice: for example, a user closing the website while making the connection will result in you losing the Item ID of that connection, meaning you'll never be able to retrieve the Item data.

### Summary

|                              | Callbacks                          | Webhooks                                                                 |
| :--------------------------- | :--------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Where to use them            | Frontend                           | Backend                                                                  |
| How information is delivered | JavaScript callback function calls | HTTP POST requests                                                       |
| Purpose                      | Improve UX                         | Deliver notifications to your backend when Pluggy-related events happen  |

## Updating an Item

Source: https://docs.pluggy.ai/en/docs/connect-widget/updating-item.md

## Overview

After creating an Item successfully, you can continue to collect products data that appears in the following days by triggering an update for your existing Item reference, instead of creating a whole new Item from scratch.

Updating an existing Item is more cost-efficient, as it only retrieves institution products data generated after the last collection process.

## How to Update an Item

To update an existing Item using Pluggy Connect, follow these steps:

### 1. Create a Connect Token with the Item ID

Create a new Connect Token, specifying the `itemId` parameter of the corresponding Item connection you want to refresh. This is necessary to let Pluggy properly validate that you are authorized to access and update this specific Item.

```bash
curl --request POST \
  --url https://api.pluggy.ai/connect_token \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --header 'X-API-KEY: YOUR_API_KEY' \
  --data '{
    "itemId": "ITEM_ID_TO_UPDATE"
  }'
```

### 2. Pass the Connect Token and Item ID to the Widget

Pass to Connect both the recently created `connectToken` and the corresponding Item `id` through the `updateItem` property:

```javascript
import PluggyConnect from 'pluggy-connect-sdk';
```
