## Payment Screen Customization

Source: https://docs.pluggy.ai/en/docs/payments/customization.md

## Overview

When your customer opens a `paymentUrl`, they land on the Pluggy payment screen, where they choose their bank and authorize the payment. From the [Dashboard](https://dashboard.pluggy.ai), under **Payments > Customization**, you can make that screen look like your product: your company name and logo, and your colors.

The customization applies to every payment of an application: immediate Pix and Pix Automático alike, on desktop and on mobile. The amount, the recipient, the list of banks, the Open Finance information and the "Powered by Pluggy" footer are never customizable, so your customers always see the payment details as they are.

<Callout variant="info" title="Who can edit it">
Team **Owners** and **Admins** can change the customization. Other members see it read-only.
</Callout>

## Team default and per-application customization

There are two levels:

- **Team default**: applies to every application of the team, including the ones you create later. It does not belong to an environment: it applies to your sandbox and production applications alike.
- **Application customization**: the first time you save an application, it gets a customization of its own, starting from a copy of the team default. From then on, changes to the team default no longer affect it.

When your team has more than one application in the environment selected in the Dashboard, choose which one to edit with the **Application** selector below the page title. The first option, **All applications (team default)**, edits the team default. Each application shows whether it has its own customization or uses the team default, and an application with its own customization can go back to it at any time with **Use the team default**.

## What you can customize

### Company name

Shown next to the logo, at the top of the payment screen. Up to **30 characters**.

### Logo

Shown at the top of the payment screen, next to the company name. Upload a **PNG, JPG, SVG or WebP** file of up to **5 MB**. Unlike the widget, the payment screen only accepts uploaded logos, not URLs.

The file is checked by its content, so a file renamed to another extension is rejected. SVG files are cleaned before being stored: scripts and references to external files are removed, so use a self-contained SVG (an embedded picture is kept, a linked one is not shown).

Without a logo, the screen shows the first letter of your company name on your main color.

### Main color

Used on the buttons and highlights of the payment screen, with white text over it. Enter it as a six-digit hex color (`#RRGGBB`) or pick it. Use a color dark enough for that text to be easy to read: the Dashboard warns you when it is not, but it does not stop you from saving it.

### Secondary color

Also a six-digit hex color. Used on secondary buttons, with white or black text depending on which reads better, and on the details of Pix Automático payments (the recipient and the first payment). With **Follow main color** on, the secondary buttons are outlined in your main color, and the Pix Automático details use your main color's scale: the color itself, or lighter and darker shades of it, depending on where it is shown.

## Reusing your Pluggy Connect widget customization

If you already [customized the Pluggy Connect widget](/docs/connect-widget/customization), you can reuse its **company name**, **logo** and **main color** instead of entering them again. Turn on **Use the widget's** next to each field: the field shows the widget's value and keeps following it, so a change to the widget customization also changes the payment screen.

Each field chooses on its own: reusing the widget's company name does not bring in its logo or color. While a field follows the widget, the value you had entered for it is kept, and comes back when you turn **Use the widget's** off.

A field is only available for reuse when the widget customization has a value of its own for it. The widget's defaults (the default company name, the Pluggy logo and the Pluggy color) are not reused, and neither is a widget logo whose address is not `https`.

## Preview

The page shows a live preview of the payment screen as you edit, before you save. Switch between an immediate **Pix** payment and a **Pix Automático** one, and between the **desktop** and **mobile** layouts.

## When changes show up

After you save, new payment screens use the customization within **about a minute**. A customer who already has the payment screen open sees it the next time they load it.

## PIX por biometria

Source: https://docs.pluggy.ai/en/docs/payments/pix-biometric.md

With a regular [Payment Request](/docs/payments/overview), the payer is redirected to their bank on every payment to approve it. With **PIX por biometria**, the payer goes to the bank only once, to link an account to their device. From then on, they confirm each payment on the Pluggy payment page with Face ID, their fingerprint or the device's screen lock, without leaving the page.

PIX por biometria is the Open Finance *Jornada Sem Redirecionamento* (JSR). The payment is still a Pix initiated through Open Finance: it settles instantly, and you track it with the same Payment Requests, Payment Intents and webhooks you already use.

<Callout variant="info" title="Recommendation">
Read the [Payments Overview](/docs/payments/overview) first. PIX por biometria builds on the same recipients, payment requests and payment intents.
</Callout>

## How it works

### The first payment on a device

1. The payer opens the `paymentUrl` and chooses their bank. Only institutions that support linking are listed.
2. The page explains what linking means, and the payer is redirected to the bank. There they approve the link and set their limits. They have up to 15 minutes to do it.
3. Back on the payment page, the payer creates a passkey with the device's biometrics or screen lock. This completes the link.
4. The payer confirms the payment with biometrics, and the Pix is sent.

### Every later payment

On the same device and browser, the payment page finds the payer's linked account and shows it next to the payment details. The payer confirms with biometrics and the payment is sent. There is no bank redirect.

The payer can also choose to pay with another bank, which starts the first-payment path for that institution.

## Concepts

- **Payment Request**: one per purchase, created with `POST /payments/requests/pix-biometric`. You send its `paymentUrl` to the payer, as with any payment request.
- **Payment Intent**: each attempt to pay a request. PIX por biometria intents have `paymentMethod: "PIX_BIOMETRIC"` and an `enrollmentId`. Only the payment page creates them.
- **Enrollment**: the linked account. It ties the payer's account at one institution to one device and browser. Only the payer can create it, on the payment page. You can list, read and revoke enrollments through the API. See [Managing linked accounts](/docs/payments/pix-biometric-enrollments).

## Compared with a regular payment request

| | Payment Request | PIX por biometria |
|---|---|---|
| Bank redirect | On every payment | Only on the first payment on a device, to link the account |
| Where the payer confirms | In the bank's app or website | On the Pluggy payment page, with biometrics |
| Payment experience | Pluggy payment page, or your own UI through the Payment Intents API | Pluggy payment page only |
| Scheduled payments | Supported ([Pix Agendado](/docs/payments/scheduled-payments)) | Not supported: one-off payments only |
| Sandbox | Available | In development |

## Requirements and limits

- **Payment Initiation** must be enabled for your client.
- **Institutions**: the institution must support linking. Check `supportsPixBiometric` on the connector (see [Coverage](/docs/payments/coverage)).
- **Device**: the payer needs biometrics or a screen lock and a browser that supports passkeys. Some apps' built-in browsers cannot use passkeys; when the page detects one, it asks the payer to open the link in the device's browser.
- **One link per device**: a link belongs to the device and browser where the passkey was created, to the payer's CPF or CNPJ, and to your client. On another device or browser, the payer links again, which creates a new enrollment.
- **Limits**: when linking, the payer sets a per-payment and a daily limit at the bank. The institution rejects a payment above them. The enrollment's `limits` field shows them.
- **Expiration**: each link has an expiration date set by the institution (`expiresAt`). After it, the payer links again.
- **Recipients**: payments go to bank account recipients. Smart account recipients are not supported.

## Sharing balance (optional)

Create the payment request with `linkedJourney: true` to let the payer also share their account balance and overdraft limit with you when they link, in the same approval at the bank. Sharing is optional for the payer and unchecked by default. It lasts as long as the link, and you read the balance through the API before charging, to avoid payments rejected for insufficient funds. See [Managing linked accounts](/docs/payments/pix-biometric-enrollments#sharing-balance).

## Unlinking

The payer can undo a link at any time in their bank's app. You can revoke a link through the API. Either way, the next payment on that device goes through the bank again to create a new link.

See [Getting Started with PIX por biometria](/docs/payments/pix-biometric-getting-started) to create your first payment request.

## Getting Started with PIX por biometria

Source: https://docs.pluggy.ai/en/docs/payments/pix-biometric-getting-started.md

This guide takes you from a recipient to a completed PIX por biometria payment. For what PIX por biometria is and how the payer experiences it, see [PIX por biometria](/docs/payments/pix-biometric).

<Callout variant="info" title="Prerequisites">
- Payment Initiation enabled for your client.
- A [webhook](/docs/webhooks) registered for payment events, so you learn about completed payments and linked accounts without polling.
</Callout>

## 1. Create a recipient

PIX por biometria pays the same recipients as any payment request. Create a bank account recipient as shown in the [Payments Overview](/docs/payments/overview), or reuse one you already have. Smart account recipients are not supported.

## 2. Identify the payer (recommended)

Create a Payment Customer with the payer's CPF (and CNPJ for business accounts), as described in [Pre-filling the CPF/CNPJ](/docs/payments/overview#pre-filling-the-cpfcnpj), and pass its `customerId` when you create the payment request. Two things depend on it:

- The payment page uses the customer's tax number and does not ask for it. Without a customer, the payer types their CPF.
- You can list a payer's linked accounts by `customerId`. See [Managing linked accounts](/docs/payments/pix-biometric-enrollments).

## 3. Create the payment request

Create one payment request per purchase:

```json title="POST /payments/requests/pix-biometric (request)"
{
  "amount": 149.9,
  "recipientId": "ab276a3d-17ba-47eb-97bf-688475037ffe",
  "description": "Order 4821",
  "customerId": "a2d4c1e8-5b7f-4c3a-9e2d-1f6b8c0d7e55",
  "clientPaymentId": "4821",
  "linkedJourney": false,
  "callbackUrls": {
    "success": "https://my-store.com/orders/4821/paid",
    "pending": "https://my-store.com/orders/4821/pending",
    "error": "https://my-store.com/orders/4821/error"
  }
}
```

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `amount` | Yes | Amount in BRL, with up to two decimal places. Minimum `0.01`. |
| `recipientId` | Yes | The recipient that receives the payment. Bank account recipients only. |
| `description` | No | Shown to the payer. Up to 140 characters. |
| `customerId` | No | The Payment Customer that identifies the payer. Recommended. |
| `clientPaymentId` | No | Your own identifier for the payment. Up to 200 characters. |
| `linkedJourney` | No | `true` lets the payer also share their balance with you when they link. See [Sharing balance](/docs/payments/pix-biometric-enrollments#sharing-balance). Defaults to `false`. |
| `callbackUrls` | No | Where the payment page sends the payer when the payment succeeds, stays pending or fails. Same as in any payment request. |

For every field and response, see the [API reference](/reference/pix-por-biometria/payment-request-create-pix-biometric).

The response is a regular Payment Request with a `pixBiometric` object:

```json title="POST /payments/requests/pix-biometric (response)"
{
  "id": "5b7e2c1d-3a4f-4e8b-9c6d-7f0a1b2c3d4e",
  "amount": 149.9,
  "description": "Order 4821",
  "status": "CREATED",
  "createdAt": "2026-10-28T13:00:00.000Z",
  "updatedAt": "2026-10-28T13:00:00.000Z",
  "callbackUrls": {
    "success": "https://my-store.com/orders/4821/paid",
    "pending": "https://my-store.com/orders/4821/pending",
    "error": "https://my-store.com/orders/4821/error"
  },
  "paymentUrl": "https://pay.pluggy.ai/5b7e2c1d-3a4f-4e8b-9c6d-7f0a1b2c3d4e",
  "clientPaymentId": "4821",
  "pixBiometric": {
    "linkedJourney": false,
    "enrollment": null
  }
}
```

`pixBiometric.enrollment` is `null` until the request is paid. See [step 5](#5-track-the-payment).

<Callout variant="warning" title="Sandbox in development">
The PIX por biometria sandbox is in development. Until it is available, a request created with `isSandbox: true` is rejected with `PIX_BIOMETRIC_SANDBOX_NOT_SUPPORTED`. See [Testing](#testing).
</Callout>

## 4. Send the payer to the payment page

Send the payer the `paymentUrl`. The payment page handles the whole journey: choosing the bank, linking the account on the first payment, creating the passkey and confirming the payment with biometrics.

The payer must open the link in a browser that supports passkeys. Some apps' built-in browsers cannot use them; when the page detects one, it asks the payer to open the link in the device's browser.

<Callout variant="info" title="Same browser from start to end">
The first payment starts in one browser, continues at the bank and comes back to the payment page. If the bank sends the payer back to a different browser or device, the page asks them to return to where they started, or to link again from there.
</Callout>

You cannot create PIX por biometria payment intents through the API: `POST /payments/intents` answers `403` with `PIX_BIOMETRIC_INTENT_INTERNAL_ONLY` for these requests. The payment page creates them.

## 5. Track the payment

The payment request and its intents move through the usual statuses (see [Payment Intent Lifecycle and Errors](/docs/payments/intent-lifecycle)), and you get the same webhooks.

**First payment on a device** (the payer links an account):

1. `payment_intent/created`
2. `payment_intent/waiting_payer_authorization`: the payer is on their way to the bank to approve the link.
3. `pix_biometric_enrollment/authorized`: the link is complete.
4. `payment_intent/completed`

**Later payments** (the payer already has a link on that device):

1. `payment_intent/created`
2. `payment_intent/completed`

`payment_request/updated` is sent whenever the request's status changes, as with any payment request.

Once the request is paid, it shows the linked account it was paid with:

```json title="GET /payments/requests/{id} (excerpt)"
{
  "id": "5b7e2c1d-3a4f-4e8b-9c6d-7f0a1b2c3d4e",
  "status": "COMPLETED",
  "pixBiometric": {
    "linkedJourney": false,
    "enrollment": {
      "id": "c91a5e2b-7d0f-4f3e-9a51-2f6b8e1d4c77",
      "status": "AUTHORIZED",
      "connector": {
        "id": 608,
        "name": "Santander",
        "imageUrl": "https://cdn.pluggy.ai/assets/connector-icons/208.svg"
      },
      "debtor": {
        "name": "John Doe",
        "taxNumber": "***.456.789-**",
        "bankAccount": {
          "agency": "1234",
          "account": "****4821",
          "name": "Santander"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

`enrollment.status` is the link's current status, so it changes if the link is later revoked or expires. It stays `null` when the request was not paid, even if the payer created a link along the way: the `pix_biometric_enrollment/*` webhooks report that link.

Each payment intent carries `paymentMethod: "PIX_BIOMETRIC"` and the `enrollmentId` it was paid with.

### When a payment fails

Besides the payment errors in [Payment Intent Lifecycle and Errors](/docs/payments/intent-lifecycle), a PIX por biometria intent can end with one of these `errorDetail.code` values:

| Intent status | `errorDetail.code` | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `CONSENT_REJECTED` | `ENROLLMENT_REJECTED` | The institution or the payer rejected the link, so the first payment was not made. |
| `CONSENT_REJECTED` | `ENROLLMENT_NOT_COMPLETED` | The link expired or ended before the payer completed it, for example because they did not come back from the bank in time. |
| `CANCELED` | `PIX_BIOMETRIC_SUPERSEDED` | The payer started a new attempt on the same payment request, for example by choosing another bank. The new attempt continues. |

A failed attempt does not close the payment request: the payer can try again from the same `paymentUrl`.

## Errors when creating the payment request

| Status | `codeDescription` | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `400` | `PIX_BIOMETRIC_SANDBOX_NOT_SUPPORTED` | `isSandbox` was `true`. The PIX por biometria sandbox is in development. |
| `400` | `PIX_BIOMETRIC_RECIPIENT_NOT_SUPPORTED` | The recipient is a smart account. |
| `403` | `PAYMENT_INITIATION_NOT_ALLOWED` | Payment Initiation is not enabled for your client. |
| `404` | `PAYMENT_RECIPIENT_NOT_FOUND` | The `recipientId` does not exist for your client. |
| `404` | `PAYMENT_CUSTOMER_NOT_FOUND` | The `customerId` does not exist for your client. |

## Testing

The PIX por biometria sandbox is in development. Until it is available, testing means a real payment in production:

- Use a small amount, such as `0.01`.
- Pay from an account at an institution that supports linking (`supportsPixBiometric`), on a phone or computer with biometrics or a screen lock.
- Pay from an account other than the recipient's. A payment to the same account is rejected with `SAME_ORIGIN_DESTINATION_ACCOUNTS`.
- When you are done, revoke the test link with `POST /pix-biometric/enrollments/{id}/revoke`, or undo it in the bank's app.

Next: [Managing linked accounts](/docs/payments/pix-biometric-enrollments).

## Managing linked accounts

Source: https://docs.pluggy.ai/en/docs/payments/pix-biometric-enrollments.md

When a payer links an account on the payment page, Pluggy stores an **enrollment**: the link between their account at one institution and the device and browser where they created the passkey. Enrollments are created only by the payer, during a payment. Through the API you can list them, read them, see the payments made with them and revoke them.

Every endpoint on this page only returns your own client's enrollments.

## The enrollment

```json title="Enrollment"
{
  "id": "c91a5e2b-7d0f-4f3e-9a51-2f6b8e1d4c77",
  "status": "AUTHORIZED",
  "connector": {
    "id": 608,
    "name": "Santander",
    "imageUrl": "https://cdn.pluggy.ai/assets/connector-icons/208.svg"
  },
  "debtor": {
    "name": "John Doe",
    "taxNumber": "***.456.789-**",
    "bankAccount": {
      "agency": "1234",
      "account": "****4821",
      "name": "Santander"
    }
  },
  "cpf": "***.456.789-**",
  "cnpj": null,
  "customerId": "a2d4c1e8-5b7f-4c3a-9e2d-1f6b8c0d7e55",
  "limits": {
    "transaction": 1000,
    "daily": 3000,
    "dailyUsed": 149.9
  },
  "expiresAt": "2027-10-28T13:05:00.000Z",
  "dataConsent": null,
  "revokedBy": null,
  "errorDetail": null,
  "createdAt": "2026-10-28T13:02:00.000Z",
  "updatedAt": "2026-10-28T13:05:00.000Z"
}
```

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `id` | The enrollment id. Payment intents reference it as `enrollmentId`. |
| `status` | See the table below. |
| `connector` | The institution where the account is held. |
| `debtor` | The linked account, as the institution reported it. The tax number and the account number are masked. |
| `cpf` / `cnpj` | The payer's tax number, masked. Use the unmasked value to [filter the list](#list-enrollments). |
| `customerId` | The Payment Customer of the payment request where the link was created, or `null` when the payer typed their CPF. |
| `limits` | The per-payment (`transaction`) and `daily` limits the payer set at the bank, and how much of today's limit is used (`dailyUsed`), in BRL. Any of them can be `null` when the institution does not report it. |
| `expiresAt` | When the link expires, as set by the institution. |
| `dataConsent` | The balance-sharing permission, or `null` when it was not requested. See [Sharing balance](#sharing-balance). |
| `revokedBy` | Who revoked the link: `BANK` (the payer or the institution, at the bank) or `CLIENT` (you, through the API). `null` unless `status` is `REVOKED`. |
| `errorDetail` | `{ code, description }` with the reason the institution gave when the link was rejected, for example because the payer did not complete it in time. Otherwise `null`. |

| `status` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `CREATED` | The payer started linking and has not finished: they are at the bank or creating the passkey. |
| `AUTHORIZED` | The link is active. Payments on that device need only biometrics. |
| `REJECTED` | The link was not completed: the institution or the payer rejected it, or the payer did not finish in time. `errorDetail` says which. |
| `REVOKED` | The link was revoked at the bank or through the API. |
| `EXPIRED` | The link reached its expiration date or became inactive at the institution. |

`REJECTED`, `REVOKED` and `EXPIRED` are final. To pay with biometrics again, the payer links again, which creates a new enrollment.

## List enrollments

```
GET /pix-biometric/enrollments?customerId={customerId}&status=AUTHORIZED
```

| Query parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| `customerId` | Enrollments created in payment requests for this Payment Customer. |
| `cpf` | The payer's CPF, digits only. |
| `cnpj` | The payer's CNPJ, digits only. |
| `status` | One of the statuses above. |
| `page` / `pageSize` | Pagination. `pageSize` is at most `500`. |

The response uses the usual pagination:

```json title="GET /pix-biometric/enrollments (response)"
{
  "total": 1,
  "totalPages": 1,
  "page": 1,
  "results": [
    {
      "id": "c91a5e2b-7d0f-4f3e-9a51-2f6b8e1d4c77",
      "status": "AUTHORIZED"
    }
  ]
}
```

A payer can have several enrollments: one per device and browser, and one per institution they linked. See the [API reference](/reference/pix-por-biometria/pix-biometric-enrollments-list).

## Retrieve an enrollment

```
GET /pix-biometric/enrollments/{id}
```

Returns the enrollment, refreshed from the institution, so a link revoked at the bank shows up as `REVOKED` here even before the webhook arrives. An id that does not exist for your client answers `404` with `PIX_BIOMETRIC_ENROLLMENT_NOT_FOUND`. See the [API reference](/reference/pix-por-biometria/pix-biometric-enrollment-retrieve).

## Payments made with an enrollment

```
GET /payments/intents?enrollmentId={id}
```

Lists the payment intents made with that link, with the usual pagination. Each one carries its `paymentRequest`, so you can tell which purchases the payer made with it. See the [API reference](/reference/payment-intent/payment-intents-list).

## Revoke an enrollment

```
POST /pix-biometric/enrollments/{id}/revoke
```

No body. The link is revoked at the institution and the enrollment is returned with `status: "REVOKED"` and `revokedBy: "CLIENT"`. You also get a `pix_biometric_enrollment/revoked` webhook. If the payer was still completing their first payment with that link, that payment intent fails.

Revoking cannot be undone: the payer has to link again to pay with biometrics. Revoking an enrollment that is already `REJECTED`, `REVOKED` or `EXPIRED` returns it unchanged, so retrying is safe. See the [API reference](/reference/pix-por-biometria/pix-biometric-enrollment-revoke).

The payer can also undo the link at any time in their bank's app. You learn about it through the `pix_biometric_enrollment/revoked` webhook, and the enrollment then shows `revokedBy: "BANK"`.

## Sharing balance

When the payment request was created with `linkedJourney: true`, the payer can also share their account balance and overdraft limit with you, in the same approval at the bank. It is optional for the payer and lasts as long as the link. Read the balance right before charging, to avoid a payment rejected for insufficient funds.

The enrollment carries the permission in `dataConsent`:

```json
{
  "status": "AUTHORISED",
  "rejectionReason": null,
  "updatedAt": "2026-10-28T13:05:00.000Z"
}
```

| `dataConsent.status` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `AWAITING_AUTHORISATION` | The payer has not approved yet. |
| `AUTHORISED` | The balance can be read. |
| `REJECTED` | The payer or the institution rejected it. `rejectionReason` says why. |
| `REVOKED` | The permission was cancelled. |

`dataConsent` is `null` when the request did not ask for it, or the payer chose not to share.

### Read the balance

```
GET /pix-biometric/enrollments/{id}/balance
```

Reads the balance in real time from the institution. Amounts are in BRL. See the [API reference](/reference/pix-por-biometria/pix-biometric-enrollment-balance-retrieve).

```json
{
  "balance": 5.48,
  "overdraft": {
    "contracted": 1000,
    "used": 0,
    "available": 1000
  }
}
```

`overdraft` is the account's overdraft limit: how much was contracted, how much is in use and how much is still available. It is `null` when the institution does not share it.

| Status | `codeDescription` | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | | Balance read. |
| `403` | `PIX_BIOMETRIC_DATA_CONSENT_NOT_AVAILABLE` | The link is not `AUTHORIZED`, or the payer did not share the balance, or the permission was cancelled. |
| `429` | `PIX_BIOMETRIC_RATE_LIMITED` | The institution's rate limit is reached, for example the account's monthly balance quota. |

<Callout variant="warning" title="Every call counts toward the institution's quota">
Each call reads the balance from the institution, with no cache. Open Finance limits balance reads per account per month (see [Operational Rate Limits](/docs/open-finance/rate-limits)). Read the balance right before a payment, not on a schedule.
</Callout>

### Stop sharing the balance

```
DELETE /pix-biometric/enrollments/{id}/data-consent
```

Cancels only the balance permission: the link stays `AUTHORIZED` and payments keep working. It returns the enrollment with `dataConsent.status` set to `REVOKED`. Cancelling a permission that already ended returns the enrollment unchanged, so retrying is safe. A link created without the permission answers `403` with `PIX_BIOMETRIC_DATA_CONSENT_NOT_AVAILABLE`. See the [API reference](/reference/pix-por-biometria/pix-biometric-enrollment-data-consent-delete).

Revoking the link also ends the balance permission. A permission cannot be added to an existing link: the payer links again from a payment request created with `linkedJourney: true`.

## Webhooks

| Event | When |
|---|---|
| `pix_biometric_enrollment/authorized` | The payer completed a link. |
| `pix_biometric_enrollment/revoked` | The link was revoked, at the bank or through the API. |
| `pix_biometric_enrollment/error` | The link was not completed: it was rejected, or ended before the payer finished it. |

```json title="pix_biometric_enrollment/authorized"
{
  "event": "pix_biometric_enrollment/authorized",
  "eventId": "8013240b-7c0a-409e-bf00-7fc586cc9196",
  "enrollmentId": "c91a5e2b-7d0f-4f3e-9a51-2f6b8e1d4c77",
  "customerId": "a2d4c1e8-5b7f-4c3a-9e2d-1f6b8c0d7e55",
  "paymentRequestId": "5b7e2c1d-3a4f-4e8b-9c6d-7f0a1b2c3d4e"
}
```

`paymentRequestId` is the payment request where the link was created, and `customerId` is `null` when it had no customer. Each event is sent once, when the enrollment enters that status. Retrieve the enrollment for the details.

A link that was `AUTHORIZED` and later reaches its `expiresAt` sends no event: check `expiresAt`, or retrieve the enrollment, to know it ended.

## Introduction

Source: https://docs.pluggy.ai/en/docs/smart-transfers/introduction.md

Pluggy's Smart Transfers API makes payments instant, easy, and secure. Here we describe in a simple way how you can implement it.

<Callout variant="info" title="Recommendation">
You should see our [Payment Initiation docs](/docs/payments/overview) first to understand the payments flow.
</Callout>

The main differences between this API and [Payment Initiation](/docs/payments/overview) are:

- The user only needs to give the consent one time (from now on, **Smart Transfer Preauthorization**) per debtor account: After the consent is given, you can use the Smart Transfers API to send money from this account to the authorized recipients (until the consent expires or it's revoked). This allows you to automatize your payment process without user interaction.
- All accounts (debtor and recipients) **must belong to the same owner (same CPF for PF accounts and same CNPJ for PJ accounts)**.

See the [next section](/docs/smart-transfers/preauthorization) to know how to generate a **Smart Transfer Preauthorization**.

## Creating a preauthorization

Source: https://docs.pluggy.ai/en/docs/smart-transfers/preauthorization.md

In this section, you will learn how to create a preauthorization to do payments without user interaction.

## Create a payment recipient

First, you need to create **Payment Recipients**. Those will be the allowed destinations to send transfers. All of recipients must belong to the same owner.

```shell
curl --location 'https://api.pluggy.ai/payments/recipients' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--header 'X-API-KEY: ••••••' \
--data '{
  "account": {
    "type": "CHECKING_ACCOUNT",
    "number": "1111111",
    "branch": "0001"
  },
  "paymentInstitutionId": "abfd2a88-bc7b-407f-9fcc-395548ee6840",
  "name": "John Doe",
  "taxNumber": "11111111111"
}'
```

Check the [API docs](/reference/payment-recipient/payment-recipient-create) to know how to use this endpoint. To know the `paymentInstitutionId`, you need to use this [endpoint](/reference/payment-recipient/payment-recipients-institution-list).

This will return the following response:

```json
{
  "type": "BANK_ACCOUNT",
  "id": "ded2e966-bd40-4e82-b467-d32fe4b4f40e",
  "name": "John Doe",
  "taxNumber": "11111111111",
  "isDefault": false,
  "paymentInstitution": {
    "id": "abfd2a88-bc7b-407f-9fcc-395548ee6840",
    "name": "Banco XP S.A.",
    "tradeName": "BCO XP S.A.",

  },
  "pixKey": null,

  "updatedAt": "2024-08-01T16:32:29.276Z"
}
```

## Create the Smart Transfer Preauthorization

Now, you are ready to create a smart transfer preauthorization. To do that, you need to do the following request:

```shell
curl --location 'https://api.pluggy.ai/smart-transfers/preauthorizations' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--header 'X-API-KEY: ••••••' \
--data '{
  "connectorId": 612,
  "parameters": {
    "cpf": "11111111111"
  },
  "recipientIds": [
    "ded2e966-bd40-4e82-b467-d32fe4b4f40e"
  ],
  "callbackUrls": {
    "success": "https://my-success-page.com",
    "error": "https://my-error-page.com"
  },
  "configuration": {
    "transactionLimit": 100
  },
  "linkedJourney": true
}'
```

- The `connectorId` will be the one associated with the institution of your debtor account (for example, if you want to create the preauthorization in Nubank, you need to send the id `612`).

- You can configure the transaction limits sending the `configuration` field (see [Configuring transaction limits section](#configuring-transaction-limits)).

- **linkedJourney** (optional, default false): also ask the user, in the same approval at the bank, for permission to read the source account balance. See [Source account balance](#source-account-balance).

  For more details about this endpoint, check our [API docs](/reference/smart-transfer/smart-transfer-preauthorization-create).

<Callout variant="warning" title="Important">
For PF accounts you can only configure one recipient per authorization. Only PJ accounts can configure multiple recipients for the same authorization.
</Callout>

This will return the following response:


After the preauthorization is created, you need to redirect your user to the `consentUrl` returned in the response. There, the user needs to approve the preauthorization in their payment institution. After the consent is given, the user will be redirected to the `success` callback url if everything is ok, or to the `error` callback url if the consent was rejected or if an error happens in the process.

Note: if you don't define a set of `callbackUrls`, the user will be redirected to a Pluggy's default page.

Now, if you check the preauthorization status using [this endpoint](/reference/smart-transfer/smart-transfer-preauthorization-retrieve), you will see it with one of the following statuses:

- **COMPLETED**: The preauthorization was completed and you are ready to create payments.
- **REJECTED**: The user rejected the preauthorization in the institution consent flow.
- **ERROR**: There was an error in the institution consent flow.

In the [next section](/docs/smart-transfers/creating-payment), you will see how to create a payment without user interaction.

## Configuring transaction limits

You can configure the transaction limits sending the `configuration` object.

| Field | Type | Optional | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| totalAllowedAmount | number | true | Maximum amount to be reached by the sum of all transactions that use the consent authorized by the customer. |
| transactionLimit | number | true | Maximum amount for each payment transaction associated with this consent. |
| periodicLimits | object | true | Transactional limits per period as determined by the paying user. |

In the `periodicLimits` object, you can configure the limits per period. The available periods are `day`, `week`, `month` and `year`, and for each one you can configure:

| Field | Type | Optional | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| quantityLimit | number | true | Maximum number of transactions allowed to occur in the period. |
| transactionLimit | number | true | Maximum amount to be transacted in the period. |

Example:

```json
{
  "configuration": {
    "totalAllowedAmount": 100.5,
    "transactionLimit": 10,
    "periodicLimits": {
      "day": {
        "quantityLimit": 2,
        "transactionLimit": 5
      },
      "week": {
        // week limits
      },
      "month": {
        // month limits
      },
      "year": {
        // year limits
      }
    }
  }
}
```

In the case that some limit is reached, you will receive an appropriate error from the API.

## Source account balance

Smart Transfers are paid from the user's account without a new approval, so a transfer can be rejected for insufficient balance. Create the preauthorization with `linkedJourney: true` to also ask the user, in the same approval at the bank, for permission to read the source account balance. Nothing else changes in the redirect, the return or the transfers.

### Permission status

The preauthorization carries a `dataConsent` object while the permission exists. It is `null` when `linkedJourney` was not requested, and it can also be `null` when the balance permission is not available for that institution or environment. In that case the preauthorization is created normally, without the permission.

| `status` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `AWAITING_AUTHORISATION` | The user has not approved yet. |
| `AUTHORISED` | The balance can be read. |
| `REJECTED` | Rejected, revoked, cancelled or expired. It does not come back; `rejectionReason` says why. |

The permission ends with the preauthorization. If the user revokes either one from their bank, the balance endpoint answers `403`, and the stored status can still read `AUTHORISED` until the institution reports the change.

`dataConsent` is refreshed from the institution when you retrieve the preauthorization by id. The list returns the last known status. `updatedAt` is when Pluggy last saw the status change.

### Read the balance

`GET /smart-transfers/preauthorizations/{id}/balance` reads the source account balance in real time from the institution. Amounts are in BRL.

```json
{
  "balance": 5.48,
  "overdraft": {
    "contracted": 1000,
    "used": 0,
    "available": 1000
  }
}
```

`overdraft` is the account's overdraft limit: how much was contracted, how much is in use and how much is still available. It is `null` when the institution does not share it.

| Status | `codeDescription` | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | | Balance read. |
| `400` | `SMART_TRANSFER_DATA_CONSENT_NOT_REQUESTED` | The preauthorization was created without `linkedJourney`. |
| `403` | `SMART_TRANSFER_DATA_CONSENT_NOT_AVAILABLE` | The permission is pending, rejected or revoked. |
| `429` | `BALANCE_OPEN_FINANCE_RATE_LIMIT` | The rate limit at the institution is reached, for example the account's monthly balance quota. |

<Callout variant="warning" title="Every call counts toward the institution's quota">
Each call reads the balance from the institution, with no cache. Open Finance limits balance reads per account per month (see [Operational Rate Limits](/docs/open-finance/rate-limits)). Read the balance right before a transfer, not on a schedule.
</Callout>

### Cancel only the permission

`DELETE /smart-transfers/preauthorizations/{id}/data-consent` cancels the balance permission and returns the preauthorization with `dataConsent.status` set to `REJECTED`. The preauthorization stays active and its transfers keep working. A permission cannot be added to an existing preauthorization: create a new one with `linkedJourney`.

| Status | `codeDescription` | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | | Permission cancelled, or it had already ended. |
| `400` | `SMART_TRANSFER_DATA_CONSENT_NOT_REQUESTED` | The preauthorization was created without `linkedJourney`. |
| `403` | `SMART_TRANSFER_DATA_CONSENT_NOT_AVAILABLE` | The institution did not accept the cancellation, for example because the user has not approved the permission yet. |
| `429` | `BALANCE_OPEN_FINANCE_RATE_LIMIT` | The rate limit at the institution is reached. |

Cancelling a permission that already ended (rejected, revoked, or its preauthorization revoked or rejected) answers `200` with `status: REJECTED`, so retrying is safe.

## Creating a payment

Source: https://docs.pluggy.ai/en/docs/smart-transfers/creating-payment.md

In this section, you will learn how to create a payment associated with a Smart Transfer Preauthorization.

To create a payment, you need to do the following request:

```shell
curl --location 'https://api.pluggy.ai/smart-transfers/payments' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--header 'X-API-KEY: ••••••' \
--data '{
  "preauthorizationId": "7e3e1dbb-8009-4966-9254-1eaab05ad18b",
  "recipientId": "ded2e966-bd40-4e82-b467-d32fe4b4f40e",
  "amount": 100,
  "description": "My automatic payment"
}'
```

Let's analyze the fields we need to send:

- `preauthorizationId`: It is the id of the preauthorization we created in the [previous section](/docs/smart-transfers/preauthorization).
- `recipientId`: It is one of the recipients we authorized for the given preauthorization. Other recipients will be rejected.
- `amount`: The amount you want to send.
- `description`: An optional description to send with the transfer.

For more details about this endpoint, check the [API docs](/reference/smart-transfer/smart-transfer-payment-create).

This will return the following:

```json
{
  "id": "b2b132f7-4c17-4707-bd5d-197d71d01385",
  "preauthorizationId": "7e3e1dbb-8009-4966-9254-1eaab05ad18b",
  "status": "CONSENT_AUTHORIZED",
  "amount": 100,
  "description": "My automatic payment",
  "recipient": {
    "type": "BANK_ACCOUNT",
    "id": "ded2e966-bd40-4e82-b467-d32fe4b4f40e",
    "name": "John Doe",
    "taxNumber": "11111111111",
    "isDefault": false,
    "paymentInstitution": {
      "id": "abfd2a88-bc7b-407f-9fcc-395548ee6840",
      "name": "Banco XP S.A.",
      "tradeName": "BCO XP S.A.",
      "ispb": "33264668",
      "compe": "348",
      "createdAt": "2023-12-08T17:52:21.001Z",
      "updatedAt": "2023-12-08T17:52:21.001Z"
    },
    "account": {
      "type": "CHECKING_ACCOUNT",
      "number": "1111111",
      "branch": "0001"
    },
    "pixKey": null,
    "createdAt": "2024-07-31T15:56:03.938Z",
    "updatedAt": "2024-07-31T15:56:23.123Z"
  },
  "createdAt": "2024-08-01T17:03:12.278Z",
  "updatedAt": "2024-08-01T17:03:15.419Z",
  "clientPaymentId": null

```

You can use [this endpoint](/reference/smart-transfer/smart-transfer-paymentretrieve) to know when the payment is completed (it generally takes a few seconds). If everything is ok, the payment status will be `PAYMENT_COMPLETED`.

<Callout variant="info" title="About transfer limits">
Smart Transfers are categorized as an Immediate Pix between different accounts of the same holder. Therefore, the limits defined in the consent for this product should be treated the same way the institution applies the limits of the Pix arrangement.

The calculation of the periodic limit available to the customer should follow the guidelines below, considering different scenarios and examples:

**Daily Limit (e.g., R$ 100.00)**: This limit controls transfers made within a single day, considering the period from 00:00 to 23:59. For example, if a user transfers R$ 50.00 at 10:00, they will still have R$ 50.00 available for transfers until midnight of the same day;

**Weekly Limit (e.g., R$ 1,000.00)**: The weekly limit covers the period of an entire week, starting at 00:00 on Sunday and ending at 23:59 on Saturday. For example, if a user transfers R$ 200.00 on Tuesday and R$ 500.00 on Thursday, they will still have R$ 300.00 available for transfers until the end of Saturday;

**Monthly Limit (e.g., R$ 10,000.00)**: This monthly limit is calculated from the first to the last day of each month. For example, in a month, if the user transfers R$ 2,000.00 in the first week and R$ 3,000.00 in the second week, they will still have R$ 5,000.00 available for transfers for the rest of the month;

**Annual Limit (e.g., R$ 50,000.00)**: The annual limit counts from the first day of January to the last day of December. For example, if a user transfers R$ 10,000.00 by March, another R$ 15,000.00 by June, and another R$ 20,000.00 by September, they will only be able to transfer another R$ 5,000.00 until the end of the year.

These limits help manage fund transfers, ensuring they do not exceed the amounts set for each period. Each limit is independent and is recalculated as its respective time window resets.
</Callout>

## Basic concepts

Source: https://docs.pluggy.ai/en/docs/developer-tools/basic-concepts.md

## Security protocols

Pluggy's API enforces the use of HTTPS TLSv1.2 or upper versions for security reasons. Other TLS version requests will be rejected. All communication requires to be in HTTPS.

## API verbs and Protocols

Pluggy's API is a RESTful API based on JSON requests and responses, so all requests must have set the header `Content-Type` of `application/json`.

We follow the RESTful standards and all verbs match their specific action for the resource you will be communicating.

<Callout variant="info" title="API response fields">
We evolve our API in a non-breaking way, by adding new fields to our endpoint responses. This makes it simpler since there are no complicated versioning mechanisms, but it also means that your HTTP client must support receiving unknown fields in a response and ignore them. In most libraries this is supported by default, but please review your particular case to check that this is configured correctly.
</Callout>

## Environment

Our production environment is accepting requests in the following host:

```
https://api.pluggy.ai
```

## Request IDs

Every response from the Pluggy API carries an `x-request-id` header — a UUID
identifying that single request:

```
x-request-id: 079482e5-8aa4-4708-9aaa-43c2f2792b4a
```

It is on every response, successful or not, and it is the one value that lets us
find your exact request in our logs. Reading it costs nothing:

```bash
curl -i https://api.pluggy.ai/connectors \
  -H 'X-API-KEY: YOUR_API_KEY' | grep -i x-request-id
```

**Log it alongside your own errors.** When something fails — a 4xx you did not
expect, a request that timed out, a response whose contents look wrong — send us
the `x-request-id` with your report. Without it we search by item, by time
window and by endpoint and often find several candidates; with it we go straight
to the request you saw, which is usually the difference between an answer the
same day and a conversation over several.

## Pagination

Some Pluggy's responses can yield a large amount of data, in which cases the size of the response is limited and divided in pages.

For example, if you make a request to `/transaction?accountId={ACCOUNT_ID}`, you will receive an object like:

```json
{
  "total": 200,
  "totalPages": 15,
  "results": [],
  "page": 1
}
```

- **total**: the size of the data of the request
- **totalPages**: the total number of pages encompassing all available records
- **results**: the content of the current page
- **page**: the number of the current page

For example, `/transaction?accountId={ACCOUNT_ID}&page=2` is the second page of transactions results.

By retrieving `/transaction?accountId={ACCOUNT_ID}`, then `/transaction?accountId={ACCOUNT_ID}&page=2`, and so on, you may access to all the data available, one page at a time.

To sum up, to obtain all the data from a paginated endpoint, after your first request you should iterate as many times as `totalPages`, making a new request and changing the `page` query param.

## Connect an account

Source: https://docs.pluggy.ai/en/docs/developer-tools/connect-account.md

In this section, we will learn how to connect the Pluggy API with a financial institution.

Each financial entity will have a connector and specific payloads necessary for the connection that must be completed in the body of the request in Postman.

These required payloads are found in the List Connectors (`GET /connectors`) response, in the `credentials` field inside each Connector object. Each of these credentials represents the structure definition for each parameter that needs to be sent, to solve the login step.

There are connectors that also require an additional Multi-factor Authentication (MFA) parameter. We have two possible scenarios here:

1. The MFA parameter can be solved by the user alone without a prompt from the financial institution, for example with Google Authenticator. In this scenario, the parameter will be found inside the `credentials` payload, it will have the field `"mfa": true` set. It has to be sent in the initial login step.

2. The MFA parameter can only be solved by the user by completing a challenge generated by the financial institution, such as a token sent by email or SMS, scanning a QR code, or answering some other prompt. The details to solve this parameter will be found after successfully logging in, in the Retrieve Item (`GET /items/:id`) response, in the `parameter` payload. Then, the parameter value has to be sent with the Send Item MFA (`POST /items/:id/mfa`) endpoint.

Connectors with this scenario can be distinguished with the field `"mfa": true` at the base of the connector payload definition.

Therefore, we will divide the connectors to facilitate understanding:

- Connectors without verification code
- Connectors with one-step verification code ("MFA 1-step")
- Connectors with two-step verification code ("MFA 2-step")

## Connectors without verification code

To connect an account that does not need an extra validation code, simply access the Postman Collection, expand the "Items" folder and select the "Create Item" request.

On the "Body" tab, enter your credentials in the elements presented in the "Create Item" request.

We list each of the institutions and their specificities below:

### Itau PF

```json
{
  "connectorId": 201,
  "parameters": {
    "agency": "",
    "account": "",
    "password": ""
  },
  "clientUserId": ""
}
```

<Callout variant="info">
For Itau PF to recover Payment Data, it's necessary to update the item at least once.
For Itau PF with joint account (conta conjunta) please see below (Exception Flows).
</Callout>

### Santander PF

```json
{
  "connectorId": 208,
  "parameters": {
    "user": "<cpf>",
    "password": ""
  },
  "clientUserId": ""
}
```

### Agora

```json
{
  "connectorId": 220,
  "parameters": {
    "cpf": "",
    "password": "",
    "signature": ""
  },
  "clientUserId": ""
}
```

### Genial

```json
{
  "connectorId": 213,
  "parameters": {
    "email": "",
    "password": ""
  },
```

## Connectors with one-step verification code ("MFA 1-step")

To connect an account that requests an extra validation code in a single login step, simply access the Postman Collection, expand the "Items" folder and select the "Create Item with MFA" request.

In the "Body" tab, your credentials to access the institution must be inserted together with the verification code (token, SMS, etc), as presented in the elements of the "Create Item with MFA" request.

<Callout variant="info" title="Connector &quot;MFA 1-step&quot;">
You can detect which institutions are included in this scenario, by finding the `"mfa": true` value, in one of the `credentials` objects, inside the connectors in the List Connectors response.
</Callout>

## Connectors with two-step verification code ("MFA 2-step")

In this flow, the parameter for inserting verifier code will be requested after the user's credentials are validated. Thus, it is necessary to send the credentials and wait for validation so that the verification code can be sent.

<Callout variant="info" title="Connector &quot;MFA 2-step&quot;">
You can detect which institutions are included in this scenario, by finding the `"mfa": true` value, at the base definitions of a Connector, found in the List Connectors response.
</Callout>

To check if the credentials have been validated and the verification code must already be sent, just access the Postman Collection, expand the "Items" folder, select the "Specific Item" request and insert the `item_id` as a parameter of the URL. In the service response, the token must be sent when the `status` and `executionStatus` elements have the value `WAITING_USER_INPUT`.

At this point, the verification code must be sent in order for the connection to be established. To send the code, simply access the Postman Collection, expand the "Items" folder and select the "Send MFA Parameter user-triggered" request.

In the "Body" tab, the verification code must be inserted as shown in the elements of the "Send MFA Parameter user-triggered" request (token, sms, etc).

## Connectors with Company Selection

The business connectors may require you to select which company you want to connect with, depending on if the user that is accessing has access to more than one single company.

In those cases, after initializing the item with the initial parameters you will be prompted with an additional parameter.

This parameter can be recovered from "Specific Item" endpoint, sending the id created, and will be of type `select` -- this means that one of the list values must be sent back to us for selection.

### Sicoob PJ

```json
{
  "id": "a9481a68-38cc-4433-bfcc-dafc05022c60",
  "status": "WAITING_USER_INPUT",
  "executionStatus": "WAITING_USER_INPUT",
  "lastUpdatedAt": null,
  "error": null,
  "paramater": {
    "type": "select",
    "name": "selectedCompany",
    "label": "Qual e a sua empresa?",
    "instructions": "Selecione a conta que deseja conectar",
    "options": [
      {
        "value": "9025000",
        "label": "902.500-0 One Company ltda"
      },
      {
        "value": "9025001",
        "label": "902.500-1 Second Company ltda"
      }
    ],
    "expiresAt": "2023-03-28T18:17:59.532Z"
  }
}
```

Once the user has selected the company, send it back using the Send MFA Endpoint:

```json
{
  "selectedCompany": "9025000"
}
```

## Exception flows

### Bradesco PF Conta Conjunta

The connector "Bradesco PF" is mapped to both simple (individual) and joint accounts (Conta Conjunta).

To connect to the joint account, you can just send any random "token" value in the endpoint "Create Item with MFA", for example `"000000"`, it won't matter because the Account selection step, if applies, will take precedence and is going to be resolved first.

```json
{
  "connectorId": 203,
  "parameters": {
    "agency": "",
    "account": "",
    "password": "",
    "token": "000000"
  },
  "clientUserId": ""
}
```

Make calls on the "Specific Item" endpoint passing the ItemId to check the status of the connection until you get the `parameter` element in the response with the `options` element which contains the list of accounts registered at the institution.

Then call the "Send MFA Parameter user-triggered" endpoint with the selected account value. After that, the token MFA parameter will need to be provided with the correct user-provided value.

Resume making calls on the "Specific Item" endpoint until the `executionStatus` attribute is set to `SUCCESS` (or `PARTIAL_SUCCESS`), meaning your connection has been created/updated successfully.

<Callout variant="info" title="Data recovered">
As this is a joint account, keep in mind that Pluggy will only collect the data from the account selected by the user on the first step.
</Callout>

### Banco do Brasil PJ

In the case of Banco do Brasil Empresas, in order for the connection to be established, it will be necessary to use a computer that is the same as the one already authorized in internet banking. The account used for the connection must have a cell phone registered with Banco do Brasil, as this will receive a confirmation link to be inserted at the time of connection.

First, make a call on the "Create Item" endpoint:

```json
{
  "connectorId": 217,
  "parameters": {
    "userJ": "",
    "passwordJ": "",
    "password": ""
  },
  "clientUserId": ""
}
```

Call the "Specific Item" endpoint until you get `executionStatus` as `WAITING_USER_INPUT` and the `parameter` attribute with a list of cell phones registered at the institution. Select a phone, then provide the SMS token URL received on that phone.

### Itau PF (Conta Conjunta)

First, make a call on the "Create Item" endpoint:

```json
{
  "connectorId": 201,
  "parameters": {
    "agency": "",
    "account": "",
    "password": ""
  },
  "clientUserId": ""
}
```

Then, call the "Specific Item" endpoint until you get the `executionStatus` as `WAITING_USER_INPUT`. The `parameter` element will include a list of accounts (operators). Select one and send it via the "Send MFA Parameter user-triggered" endpoint.

<Callout variant="info">
This parameter `operatorNumber` is asked only for the first time the Item is created, then it is stored and reutilized for any subsequent updates of the same Item instance.
</Callout>

### Itau PF (with MFA)

Some accounts from Itau PF require MFA. Create the item with the standard credentials, then poll the "Specific Item" endpoint until `WAITING_USER_INPUT` with `"name": "mfa"` in the parameter. Send the MFA token via the "Send MFA Parameter user-triggered" endpoint.

### Itau PJ

The "Itau" connector is mapped to both simple (individual) and joint accounts. To connect to the joint account, send the name of the account holder via the "Send MFA Parameter user-triggered" endpoint.

```json
{
  "connectorId": 218,
  "parameters": {
    "agency": "",
    "account": "",
    "password": "",
    "cpfOrOperator": ""
  },
  "clientUserId": ""
}
```

### XP (CPF access - joint account)

The "XP" connector allows connecting both simple accounts (account number access) and joint accounts (with CPF access).

```json
{
  "connectorId": 202,
  "parameters": {
    "account": "",
    "password": "",
    "token": ""
  },
  "clientUserId": ""
}
```

Poll the "Specific Item" endpoint until `WAITING_USER_INPUT` with a `selectedAccount` parameter, then send the selected account value.

### Santander PJ

For Santander PJ, the connection requires scanning a QR code and sending an extra validation code.

```json
{
  "connectorId": 221,
  "parameters": {
    "agency": "",
    "account": "",
    "user": "",
    "password": ""
  },
  "clientUserId": ""
}
```

Poll the "Specific Item" endpoint until `WAITING_USER_INPUT`. The `parameter` will contain a base64 encoded QR code image in the `data` attribute. Display the QR code, scan it with a phone, and send the resulting token via the "Send MFA Parameter user-triggered" endpoint.

### Inter PJ

This connector uses the bank's OAuth 2 API. You need to first generate and obtain `clientId`, `clientSecret`, the files `API_Chave.key` and `API_Certificado.crt` from the client's home banking account.

The private key and certificate should be provided as base64 without line breaks between each file's header and footer.

```json
{
  "connectorId": 225,
  "parameters": {
    "clientId": "",
    "clientSecret": "",
    "privateKey": "",
    "certificate": ""
  },
  "clientUserId": ""
}
```

### BTG Pactual, Empiricus and EQI

The "BTG" (Empiricus and EQI) connector is mapped to both simple and joint accounts. To connect to the joint account, send the name of the account holder via the "Send MFA Parameter user-triggered" endpoint.

### Safra

To connect an account, this connector requires the user to authorize a new device (`Pluggy - yyyy-mm-dd hh-mm`) through the Safra mobile app.

First, use the "Create Item" endpoint and send the necessary parameters for connection:

```json
{
  "connectorId": 229,
  "parameters": {
    "agency": "",
    "account": "",
    "password": ""
  }
}
```

If everything is ok, after entering the token provided by the Safra app, the connector will return the `executionStatus` `WAITING_USER_ACTION`. Use the "Specific Item" endpoint (`GET /items/:id`) to check the connection status. Call the endpoint until the response attribute `executionStatus` has the value `WAITING_USER_ACTION`, just like in the example below:

```json
{
  "id": "c33872c7-85dc-4d67-b262-6490d85ea2d3",
  "connector": {
    "id": 229,
    "name": "Safra",
    "primaryColor": "#00003C",
    "institutionUrl": "https://www.safra.com.br/",
    "country": "BR",
    "type": "PERSONAL_BANK",
    "credentials": [
      {
        "validation": "^\\d{3,3}\\d$",
        "validationMessage": "O agência deve ter 4 números.",
        "label": "Agência",
        "name": "agency",
        "type": "number",
        "placeholder": "Exemplo: 1234",
        "optional": false
      },
      {
        "validation": "^\\d{6,6}-?\\d$",
        "validationMessage": "A conta deve ter 7 números.",
        "label": "Conta",
        "name": "account",
        "type": "number",
        "placeholder": "Exemplo: 12345-6",
        "optional": false
      },
      {
        "validation": "^\\d{1,6}$",
        "validationMessage": "A senha deve ter menos de 6 números.",
        "label": "Senha",
        "name": "password",
        "type": "password",
        "placeholder": "",
        "optional": false
      }
    ],
    "imageUrl": "https://cdn.pluggy.ai/assets/connector-icons/229.svg",
    "hasMFA": true,
    "health": {
      "status": "ONLINE",
      "stage": null
    },
    "products": [
      "ACCOUNTS",
      "TRANSACTIONS",
      "INVESTMENTS"
    ],
    "createdAt": "2022-11-04T21:12:51.716Z"
  },
  "createdAt": "2023-02-27T17:42:40.521Z",
  "updatedAt": "2023-02-27T17:43:47.114Z",
  "status": "WAITING_USER_ACTION",
  "executionStatus": "WAITING_USER_ACTION",
  "lastUpdatedAt": null,
  "webhookUrl": null,
  "error": null,
  "clientUserId": null,
  "statusDetail": null,
  "parameter": null,
  "userAction": {
    "instructions": "User needs to authorize the device in their Safra App",
    "attributes": {
      "deviceNickname": "Pluggy - 2023-02-27 17:42"
    },
    "expiresAt": "2023-02-27T17:45:46.237Z"
  },
  "nextAutoSyncAt": null
}
```

The Item will remain in that state until:

- The user authorizes the device in the Safra app: in this case, the Item status will change automatically and a new token will be requested from the user.

or

- The user doesn't authorize the device in the Safra app: the Item will return the execution status `USER_AUTHORIZATION_NOT_GRANTED`.

or

- The current date is after the `expiresAt` date returned in the `userAction` property: the Item will return the status `USER_AUTHORIZATION_PENDING`. In this scenario, the user can authorize the device later, and after that the Item can be updated.

This flow will happen only on Item creation. If the device was authorized and the Item is updated, it will only request a token from the user.

### Banco Inter PF

Using this connector for an Item in the first execution requires the user to authorize the login with Inter by scanning a QR code with their Inter mobile app.

To do so, the user must be prepared to scan the QR code by logging in to the mobile app and going to Options → iSafe e Internet Banking → QR Code.

First, use the "Create Item" endpoint — no parameters necessary, since the entire login flow will be by QR:

```json
{
  "connectorId": 215,
  "parameters": {}
}
```

Then, return to the "Specific Item" endpoint so you can check the connection status. Soon after creation, the Item will reach a `WAITING_USER_ACTION` status. At this point, the `userAction.attributes.data` field of the Item will contain a QR code in base64 to be scanned:

```json
{
  "createdAt": "2023-02-27T12:46:25.707Z",
  "updatedAt": "2023-02-27T12:46:33.365Z",
  "status": "WAITING_USER_ACTION",
  "executionStatus": "WAITING_USER_ACTION",
  "lastUpdatedAt": null,
  "webhookUrl": null,
  "error": null,
  "clientUserId": null,
  "statusDetail": null,
  "parameter": null,
  "userAction": {
    "instructions": "SCAN QR",
    "expiresAt": 123456789,
    "attributes": {
      "name": "qr",
      "data": "data:image/png;base64,"
    }
  },
  "nextAutoSyncAt": null
}
```

Since we return the image in base64, you'll need to render it so the client can scan it. Once the user successfully scans the login QR with their mobile app, the login flow will continue normally.

<Callout variant="warning" title="Important info and recommendation">
Take in mind that the QR code expires in 5 seconds, and the Item info will be updated with a new QR code. As such, you'll need to poll the "Specific Item" endpoint to check for updates to the code. Given the very short expiration time, it's easy to render an expired QR code. So, we recommend polling every 1 second until the status of the Item changes.
</Callout>

### XP Wealth

This connector also allows you to specify which customers you want to collect financial data from. To do that, you need to send a credential `selectedCustomers` with all customer codes you want to connect, separated by commas.

```json
{
  "connectorId": 248,
  "parameters": {
    "clientId": "clientId",
    "clientSecret": "clientSecret",
    "selectedCustomers": "409185,551175,176189"
  },
  "webhookUrl": "https://www.myapi.com/notifications"
}
```

<Callout variant="warning" title="Important">
This customization is not available in our widget; you need to create the Item using the Pluggy API.
</Callout>

### Mercado Bitcoin

This connector requires creating an API Key (chave de API) in the institution account. To do that, follow [this tutorial](https://suporte.mercadobitcoin.com.br/hc/pt-br/articles/360040781391-Como-gerar-uma-chave-de-API). After that, use the client id and client secret to create an Item.

## Connectors with OAuth

OAuth connections require the user to provide authorization directly inside the Financial Institution's application, so there is a redirect flow that needs to happen between Pluggy and the FI, back and forth.

### OAuth v1

The first implementation Pluggy provided returns an `oauthUrl` on the [List Connectors](/reference/connectors-list) endpoint that is necessary to redirect the user to provide consent.

```json
{
  "id": 206,
  "name": "Mercado Pago",
  "oauthUrl": "https://auth.mercadopago.com.br/authorization?client_id=3960514748228649&redirect_uri=https://api.pluggy.ai/connectors/206/oauth/callback&response_type=code&platform_id=mp&scopes=read,offline_access&state=27364b4a-354e-479d-89bd-05cef476e1f4"
}
```

If the connector provides the `oauthUrl`, you will be required to redirect the user to that page, and after they authorize Pluggy, we will redirect them back to your application.

This affects the connectors: "MercadoPago".

### OAuth v2

After improving the flow from the previous version, we launched the integration directly through the Item, to provide better tracking of the connection attempts for our customers. Now connectors don't return the URL; instead, they don't require any credential to start the execution, and have an `oauth` flag to indicate that these connectors authenticate through OAuth.

```json
{
  "id": 200,
  "name": "MeuPluggy",
  "credentials": [],
  "oauth": true
}
```

Once the execution has started, we will provide the `oauthUrl` as a parameter for the user to be redirected. The URL may not be in the `POST /items` response: it can take a few more seconds to appear, so poll [GET /items/\{id\}](/reference/items-retrieve) until the item's parameter of type `oauth` carries it:

```json
{
  "id": "54a8d5e2-583a-40fd-a716-c9cee38a73dc",
  "parameter": {
    "label": "Oauth Code",
    "name": "oauthCode",
    "type": "oauth",
    "instructions": "Log into MeuPluggy page to continue",
    "data": "https://<institution-authorization-page>?response_type=code&redirect_uri=https://api.pluggy.ai/items/oauth/callback&state=4eb2909b-c4c5-4f68-ba2b-84f2772fb15a",
    "expiresAt": "2023-03-09T11:02:54.796Z"
  }
}
```

The parameter's type `oauth` makes it easy to understand that an OAuth flow is required, and the `data` attribute returns the URL to redirect the user to. After the callback, the Item will be created.

On updates, the flow will be the same.

## Server-Side SDKs

Source: https://docs.pluggy.ai/en/docs/developer-tools/server-sdks.md

## Server-Side SDKs

Currently, we have client libraries available for the following languages:

- [Node.js](https://github.com/pluggyai/pluggy-node)
- [.NET](https://github.com/pluggyai/pluggy-net)
- [Java](https://github.com/pluggyai/pluggy-java)

### Installation

To install the client library, use the following command:

**Node.js (npm):**

```bash
npm install --save pluggy-sdk
```

**C# (.NET):**

```powershell
Install-Package Pluggy.SDK
```

**Java (Maven):**

To install in Java, using Maven, add a dependency to your `pom.xml`:

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>ai.pluggy</groupId>
  <artifactId>pluggy-java</artifactId>
  <version>1.5.0</version>
</dependency>
```

Currently, the package is available in GitHub Packages, so make sure to have the GH Packages server config with your Personal GH Access Token in your `.m2/settings.xml` file. Navigate to [this guide](https://docs.github.com/en/packages/working-with-a-github-packages-registry/working-with-the-apache-maven-registry) for more details.

You can also do an integration yourself, by sending HTTP requests directly to our API.

<Callout variant="info" title="Interested in contributing?">
Let us know if you require or if you are interested in contributing a library for a language not represented here! Write us to hello@pluggy.ai
</Callout>

### You can also build your own one!

Using our `oas.json` which is up-to-date with all the latest endpoint definitions you can create your own integration. You can check out our OAS (Open API Specification) [here](https://api.pluggy.ai/oas3.json).

Some examples are driven by the community:

- [Python](https://github.com/diraol/pluggy-python)
