## Authentication

Source: https://docs.pluggy.ai/en/docs/reference/authentication.md

Every request carries one credential in the `X-API-KEY` header. There are two kinds, issued by two endpoints, and the difference between them is scope.

| Credential | Issued by | Lives | Reaches |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **API Key** | [`POST /auth`](/reference/auth/auth-create) | 2 hours | Every endpoint. Server-side only. |
| **Connect Token** | [`POST /connect_token`](/reference/auth/connect-token-create) | 30 minutes | The Item it was issued for and a reduced view of its Accounts. Safe to hand to a client. |

## API Key

```http
POST https://api.pluggy.ai/auth
Content-Type: application/json

{ "clientId": "…", "clientSecret": "…" }
```

Response `200`:

```json
{ "apiKey": "…" }
```

`clientId` and `clientSecret` come from the [Dashboard](https://dashboard.pluggy.ai). They identify your application, so `POST /auth` belongs on your server and nowhere else. New secrets start with `pluggy_sk_` (56 characters); secrets issued before that format have no prefix and keep working. A `401` with `codeDescription` `CLIENT_KEYS_UNAUTHORIZED` means the pair is wrong; `CLIENT_DISABLED` means the application is switched off.

The key expires **2 hours** after it is issued. Reuse it until then — `POST /auth` has its own [rate limit](/reference/rate-limits), and requesting a key per call is the usual way to hit it.

## Connect Token

```http
POST https://api.pluggy.ai/connect_token
X-API-KEY: {apiKey}
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "itemId": "…",
  "options": {
    "clientUserId": "…",
    "webhookUrl": "https://…",
    "oauthRedirectUri": "https://…",
    "avoidDuplicates": true
  }
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{ "accessToken": "…" }
```

Everything in the body is optional. `itemId` scopes the token to an existing Item, for an update. `options` are applied to every Item created with the token:

| Option | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `clientUserId` | Your identifier for the end user, stored on the Item and echoed in every `item/*` webhook. |
| `webhookUrl` | Where the events of those Items are delivered. |
| `oauthRedirectUri` | Where the user lands after an OAuth connect flow. |
| `avoidDuplicates` | Do not create a second Item for credentials that already have one. |

<Callout variant="warning" title="Options go inside options">
The only keys read at the root of the body are `itemId` and `options`. A `clientUserId` sent at the root is discarded — the call still returns `200`, and the Items end up with `clientUserId: null`. Backfill an affected Item with [`PATCH /items/{id}`](/reference/items/items-update).
</Callout>

The token expires **30 minutes** after it is issued. Issue one per connection: a new one each time you create or update an Item.

## Scope

A Connect Token is sent exactly like an API Key, in `X-API-KEY`. It can call [`GET /items/{id}`](/reference/items/items-retrieve) for its own Item and [`GET /accounts?itemId=`](/reference/account/accounts-list) with a reduced view of the data; anything else returns `403`. A token issued for one Item cannot read another, including Items created earlier with a different token.

## The flow, end to end

1. Your server calls `POST /auth` with `clientId` and `clientSecret` and keeps the API Key.
2. Your server calls `POST /connect_token` with that key and hands the `accessToken` to your client.
3. Your client — the [Connect Widget](/docs/connect-widget/introduction) or your own UI — creates or updates the Item with the token.
4. Your server reads the Item's data with the API Key.

Read the guide: [Authentication](/docs/authentication).

## Basic Concepts

Source: https://docs.pluggy.ai/en/docs/reference/basic-concepts.md

## Base URL

```
https://api.pluggy.ai
```

One environment. Test against the [Sandbox connectors](/docs/guides/sandbox) rather than a separate host.

## Transport

HTTPS with TLS 1.2 or later. Connections negotiating an older TLS version are rejected.

## Requests

REST over JSON. Send `Content-Type: application/json` on every request with a body, and the credential in `X-API-KEY` — see [Authentication](/reference/authentication). Verbs mean what they say: `GET` reads, `POST` creates, `PATCH` updates, `DELETE` removes.

## Responses

JSON. The API evolves without versions by **adding** fields to responses; nothing is removed or renamed. Your client has to accept and ignore fields it does not know — most HTTP libraries do by default, a strict deserializer may not.

Errors share one shape, whatever the endpoint:

```json
{
  "code": 401,
  "codeDescription": "CLIENT_KEYS_UNAUTHORIZED",
  "message": "Client keys are invalid"
}
```

`code` repeats the HTTP status; `codeDescription`, when present, is the stable identifier to branch on; `message` is for people. Some errors add a `data` object. The status codes are listed in [Error Codes](/reference/error-codes).

## Pagination

Two models are in use. The `v2` endpoints paginate with a cursor; every other list endpoint still paginates by page number.

Cursors are how this API paginates from here on, and page-number pagination is being phased out. Where a `v2` cursor endpoint exists, write your integration against it.

### Cursor (`v2` endpoints)

Ask for the first page with your filters. The response carries the records and `next`: a ready-made query string for the following page.

```http
GET https://api.pluggy.ai/v2/transactions
    ?accountId={ACCOUNT_ID}
X-API-KEY: {apiKey}
```

```json
{
  "results": [],
  "next": "?accountId={ACCOUNT_ID}&after={CURSOR}"
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `results` | The records of this page. |
| `next` | The query string of the next page, or `null` on the last one. |

To continue, append `next` to the endpoint path exactly as received — it already carries your filters and the `after` cursor:

```http
GET https://api.pluggy.ai/v2/transactions
    ?accountId={ACCOUNT_ID}
    &after={CURSOR}
X-API-KEY: {apiKey}
```

Never build or decode `after` yourself: the value is opaque and only valid as returned. A `null` `next` means there is nothing more to read. Cursor pagination is available on [`GET /v2/transactions`](/reference/transaction/transactions-list-by-cursor) and [`GET /v2/items`](/reference/items/items-list-by-cursor) — the latter is opt-in per team; ask support to enable it.

### Page number (other list endpoints)

Investments, investment transactions, credit card bills (`GET /bills`), payment customers, recipients and requests, and Smart Transfer pre-authorizations paginate by page:

```http
GET https://api.pluggy.ai/investments
    ?itemId={ITEM_ID}
    &page=2
    &pageSize=500
X-API-KEY: {apiKey}
```

```json
{
  "total": 200,
  "totalPages": 15,
  "page": 1,
  "results": []
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `total` | Records matching the request, across all pages. |
| `totalPages` | Pages needed to read them all. |
| `page` | The page in this response. |
| `results` | The records of this page. |

Two query parameters drive it: `page` (default `1`) and `pageSize` (default `500` where the endpoint accepts it — check the endpoint). To read everything, request `page=1`, then `page=2` … up to `totalPages`.

`page` must be an integer between 1 and 1,000,000, and `pageSize` an integer between 1 and 500. Do not rely on a larger `pageSize` being reduced to 500: most list endpoints, including `GET /items`, `GET /consents`, investments, credit card bills, payments and Smart Transfers, reject it. A value outside these ranges, or a non-numeric or empty one (`page=0`, `page=abc`, `pageSize=501`, `pageSize=`), returns `400` with `codeDescription` `INVALID_PARAMETERS`:

```json
{
  "code": 400,
  "codeDescription": "INVALID_PARAMETERS",
  "message": "pageSize must not be greater than 500"
}
```

Every list endpoint outside `v2` paginates this way today, and these are expected to gain cursor equivalents. Keep the paging logic in one place in your integration: moving an endpoint across is then a change in one function rather than at every call site.

<Callout variant="warning" title="GET /transactions is deprecated">
The page-based [`GET /transactions`](/reference/transaction/transactions-list) is **deprecated** and **available only until 2026-12-31**, as announced in the [changelog](/changelog#2026.06-transition-to-cursor-pagination-on-the-transactions-endpoint) since June 2026. Move to [`GET /v2/transactions`](/reference/transaction/transactions-list-by-cursor), which paginates by cursor as above.

Applications created on or after **2026-06-02 00:00 Brasília time (03:00 UTC)** already get `410 Gone` with `codeDescription` `ENDPOINT_DEPRECATED` from `GET /transactions`, and must use `/v2` from the start.
</Callout>

### Moving from `GET /transactions` to `GET /v2/transactions`

| `GET /transactions` | `GET /v2/transactions` |
| --- | --- |
| `accountId` | `accountId` (same) |
| `ids` | `ids`, comma-separated, up to 500 (same) |
| `from` / `to` | `dateFrom` / `dateTo` |
| `createdAtFrom` | `createdAtFrom` (same; cannot be combined with `dateFrom`) |
| `page` / `pageSize` | `after`: follow the `next` value of each response until it is `null`. Pages hold up to 500 transactions. |
| `billId`, `type`, `operationType` | Not available as filters. Every transaction still carries these fields (`billId` inside `creditCardMetadata`), so filter on your side. |
| `transactions/created` webhook: `createdTransactionsLink` | Applications created before 2026-06-02 00:00 Brasília time (03:00 UTC): use `createdTransactionsLinkV2` from the same payload. |

Read the guide: [Basic concepts](/docs/developer-tools/basic-concepts).

## Error Codes

Source: https://docs.pluggy.ai/en/docs/reference/error-codes.md

## Error body

Every error, on every endpoint, has this shape:

```json
{
  "code": 404,
  "codeDescription": "ITEM_NOT_FOUND",
  "message": "Item not found"
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `code` | The HTTP status, repeated. Always present. |
| `message` | A sentence for a person. Always present; not stable. |
| `codeDescription` | A stable identifier for the specific error, when the endpoint distinguishes several. Branch on this, not on `message`. |
| `data` | Extra detail for some errors — for instance, the Items that already exist when creating one would duplicate a connection. |

## Status codes

| Status | Meaning | Usually because |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `400` Bad Request | The request is invalid. | A missing or malformed field (`INVALID_PARAMETERS`). |
| `401` Unauthorized | The credential is missing, wrong or expired. | An API Key past its 2 hours, or wrong `clientId`/`clientSecret` on `POST /auth` (`CLIENT_KEYS_UNAUTHORIZED`, `CLIENT_DISABLED`). |
| `403` Forbidden | The credential cannot reach this resource. | A Connect Token used outside its scope — see [Authentication](/reference/authentication). |
| `404` Not Found | No such resource. | An `id` that does not exist. |
| `405` Method Not Allowed | The endpoint does not support this verb. | |
| `406` Not Acceptable | A format other than JSON was requested. | |
| `409` Conflict | The request contradicts the current state of the resource. | A conflict updating an Item — see [`PATCH /items/{id}`](/reference/items/items-update). |
| `429` Too Many Requests | A rate limit was exceeded. | See [Rate Limits](/reference/rate-limits) for the limits and the `Retry-After` header. |
| `500` Internal Server Error | Something failed on our side. | Retry later. |
| `503` Service Unavailable | Temporarily unavailable. | Maintenance, or a financial institution that is temporarily not answering (`BALANCE_INSTITUTION_RATE_LIMITED`). Retry later. |

Each endpoint's page in this reference lists the statuses it returns and, where the API distinguishes them, the `codeDescription` values.

## Invalid parameters

| `codeDescription` | Status | Message | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `INVALID_PARAMETERS` | `400` | Names the parameter and the problem — for instance `accountId must be a UUID`, `property pageSize should not exist` or `page must be an integer between 1 and 1000000`. | A path, query or body parameter is missing, malformed, or not accepted by the endpoint. Fix the parameter named in the message; retrying the same request returns the same error. |

<Callout variant="warning" title="Unknown query parameters are rejected from 2026-11-23">
Starting 2026-11-23 16:00 Brasília time (19:00 UTC), `GET` endpoints reject query parameters they do not accept with `400 INVALID_PARAMETERS` and the message `Query parameter 'x' is not accepted by this endpoint`. Before that date, unknown query parameters are silently ignored. Send only the parameters listed on each endpoint's reference page.
</Callout>

## Creating and updating an Item

These come back from [`POST /items`](/reference/items/items-create) and
[`PATCH /items/{id}`](/reference/items/items-update). Where the text below shows a
`:placeholder`, the real message carries the value — a frequency, a wait, a
parameter name.

| `codeDescription` | Status | Message | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `PARAMETERS_NOT_PROVIDED` | `400` | parameters were not provided | Send the connection's credentials to sync the item. |
| `ITEM_ALREADY_UPDATING` | `400` | An update is already in progress, wait until the last execution ends | This item is syncing. Wait for the execution to finish — success or error — before triggering another. |
| `ITEM_IS_ALREADY_UPDATING` | `400` | There is an active item for the set of credentials that hasn't finished executing | The same set of credentials is syncing on another item. Wait for it, so two sessions are not opened with the institution at once. |
| `CLIENT_IS_UPDATING_BEFORE_ALLOWED_FREQUENCY` | `409` | Client updates on this item are allowed at most every :minUpdateFrequencyAllowedInHours hours. Last update was at :lastUpdatedAt | Wait until the minimum frequency has passed since the last update. The limit is per team and adjustable — ask support if your use case needs a shorter one. |
| `LAST_EXECUTION_HAD_LOGIN_ERROR` | `400` | Last execution had a login error, you must update the parameters | The last sync failed to log in. Send new credentials before updating again. |
| `TOO_MANY_CONSECUTIVE_LOGIN_FAILURES` | `400` | must wait at least :readableBackoffTime after :maxConsecutiveFailedLoginAttempts consecutive login errors, last attempt was at :lastExecutionEndedAt (can retry after: :canRetryAfterDate) | A cooldown after repeated login errors, so the user's account is not locked by the institution. Retry after the time in the message. |
| `TOO_MANY_CONSECUTIVE_ERRORS` | `400` | There has been more than 5 failing syncronizations, please contact support | The connection failed too many times in a row. Report it to support with the `itemId`. |
| `ITEM_IN_ERROR_COOLDOWN` | `409` | This set of credentials recently failed to connect and is in a cooldown period, please try again later | These credentials failed recently and are in a cooldown. Retry after it passes. |
| `CONNECTOR_OFFLINE` | `409` | this connector is offline in this moment | The connector is not accepting executions right now. Try again later — see [status.pluggy.ai](https://status.pluggy.ai). |
| `CONNECTOR_REQUIRED_PARAMETER_VALIDATION_ERROR` | `400` | The parameter :parameter is required to be renewed for item update. | The connector now requires that parameter again. Send it to update the connection. |
| `ITEM_ORIGINAL_CONNECTED_WITH_DIFFERENT_ACCOUNT` | `409` | Item was originally connected with a different account, please use the original account | The credentials now point at a different account than the one the item was created with. Use the original account, or create a new item. |
| `ITEM_CREATION_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` | `409` | Client exceeded item creation limit (:itemsLimit items) for the current subscription level. | You reached the item limit of your subscription. The limit applies to every application that is not on a production subscription, including the Demo application created with your team; Sandbox (Pluggy Bank) items do not count towards it. Delete unused items or contact support. |
| `CLIENT_HAS_ITEM_UPDATES_DISABLED` | `409` | Client has item updates disabled | Updates were disabled for the team. Contact support. |
| `CREATE_ITEMS_API_FREE_DISABLED` | `400` | Free subscription can only create items through our Connect Widget | On the free subscription, items are created through the Connect Widget. |
| `SANDBOX_CLIENT_ITEM_UPDATE_NOT_ALLOWED` | `400` | Current client subscription level can only update Sandbox (Pluggy Bank) items | Your subscription level only allows updating Sandbox (Pluggy Bank) items. |
| `TRIAL_CLIENT_ITEM_CREATE_NOT_ALLOWED` | `400` | Trial clients can only create Sandbox (Pluggy Bank) items | During the trial, items can only be created on Sandbox (Pluggy Bank) connectors and on the [MeuPluggy](/docs/guides/meu-pluggy-personal-use) connector. Use those while on trial, or upgrade your subscription to connect other institutions. |
| `CLIENT_PLAN_REAL_CONNECTORS_NOT_ALLOWED` | `400` | Current client subscription does not allow connecting real accounts, only Sandbox (Pluggy Bank) and Meu Pluggy items | Your subscription does not allow connecting real accounts. Free applications can only connect Sandbox (Pluggy Bank) and [MeuPluggy](/docs/guides/meu-pluggy-personal-use) connectors; trial applications only list those connectors until access to real data is approved for the trial. Upgrade your subscription, or contact support, to connect other institutions. |
| `MEU_PLUGGY_ITEM_UPDATE_NOT_ALLOWED` | `400` | MeuPluggy item cant be updated | [MeuPluggy](/docs/guides/meu-pluggy-personal-use) items are kept up to date by MeuPluggy itself and cannot be updated with `PATCH /items/{id}`. Read the data with the item's endpoints; there is nothing to trigger. |

### Who has to act

Most of these share status `400`, so branch on `codeDescription`, not on the status. Only some of them need the end user, and only the "wait and retry" ones go away by retrying: the rest need a change in your request, your subscription or a support ticket. In every case, keep showing the data you already have.

This table covers every code above and every [MFA error](#mfa-errors) below.

| `codeDescription` | Requires the user | Who acts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PARAMETERS_NOT_PROVIDED` | **Yes** | The user — enters the connection's credentials. |
| `LAST_EXECUTION_HAD_LOGIN_ERROR` | **Yes** | The user — enters new credentials. |
| `CONNECTOR_REQUIRED_PARAMETER_VALIDATION_ERROR` | **Yes** | The user — provides the parameter named in the message again. |
| `ITEM_ORIGINAL_CONNECTED_WITH_DIFFERENT_ACCOUNT` | **Yes** | The user — reconnects with the original account, or creates a new item. |
| `ITEM_MFA_EXPIRED` | **Yes** | The user — starts a new update and enters a new MFA value. |
| `MFA_PARAMERTER_WAS_ALREADY_USED_ERROR` | **Yes** | The user — enters a new MFA value. |
| `ITEM_ALREADY_UPDATING` | No | Nobody — wait for the running execution and retry. |
| `ITEM_IS_ALREADY_UPDATING` | No | Nobody — wait for the other item's execution and retry. |
| `CLIENT_IS_UPDATING_BEFORE_ALLOWED_FREQUENCY` | No | Nobody — wait for the minimum frequency and retry. |
| `TOO_MANY_CONSECUTIVE_LOGIN_FAILURES` | No | Nobody — wait for the cooldown in the message and retry. |
| `ITEM_IN_ERROR_COOLDOWN` | No | Nobody — wait for the cooldown and retry. |
| `CONNECTOR_OFFLINE` | No | Nobody — retry when the connector is back online. |
| `ITEM_MFA_PARAMETER_EXPECTED_MISMATCH` | No | Your integration — send the value under the parameter name in the message. |
| `ITEM_MFA_NOT_FOUND` | No | Your integration — only send MFA while the item is waiting for it. |
| `ITEM_MFA_ALREADY_PROVIDED` | No | Your integration — nothing to send; the MFA was already received. |
| `MISSING_MFA_PARAMETER_DATA` | No | Your integration — the request had no MFA parameters; send them. |
| `MISSING_MFA_PARAMETER_VALUE` | No | Your integration — a parameter was sent empty; send the value (if the user left the field blank, ask them for it before sending). |
| `TOO_MANY_CONSECUTIVE_ERRORS` | No | Pluggy support — report it with the `itemId`. |
| `ITEM_CREATION_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` | No | Your subscription — delete unused items or contact support. |
| `CLIENT_HAS_ITEM_UPDATES_DISABLED` | No | Pluggy support. |
| `CREATE_ITEMS_API_FREE_DISABLED` | No | Your subscription — create items through the Connect Widget, or upgrade. |
| `SANDBOX_CLIENT_ITEM_UPDATE_NOT_ALLOWED` | No | Your subscription. |
| `TRIAL_CLIENT_ITEM_CREATE_NOT_ALLOWED` | No | Your subscription — use Sandbox connectors during the trial, or upgrade. |
| `CLIENT_PLAN_REAL_CONNECTORS_NOT_ALLOWED` | No | Your subscription — use Sandbox or MeuPluggy connectors, or upgrade. |
| `MEU_PLUGGY_ITEM_UPDATE_NOT_ALLOWED` | No | Your integration — don't send updates for MeuPluggy items. |

<Callout variant="info" title="Open Finance updates do not need the user">
For an Open Finance item, an update with [`PATCH /items/{id}`](/reference/items/items-update) **never needs the user**: it reads the data under the consent the user already gave. The exception is an item that already requires the user's action before the update, which you can see on the item itself:

- `status` is `WAITING_USER_ACTION` (the user still has to authorise at the institution), or `executionStatus` is `USER_AUTHORIZATION_PENDING`;
- `executionStatus` is `USER_AUTHORIZATION_REVOKED` (the user revoked the consent at the institution), `USER_AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRED` (the consent expired) or `USER_AUTHORIZATION_NOT_GRANTED` (the consent was never authorised);
- `consentExpiresAt` is in the past: the next update ends in `USER_AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRED`.

In those cases the user has to go through the institution's authorisation again — see [Consents](/docs/connections/consents).
</Callout>

## MFA errors

Returned when sending a multi-factor parameter to an Item — see
[Updating an Item](/docs/connect-widget/updating-item).

| `codeDescription` | Status | Message | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ITEM_MFA_NOT_FOUND` | `404` | item has no mfa input request | The item is not waiting for an MFA input, so none can be submitted. |
| `ITEM_MFA_ALREADY_PROVIDED` | `400` | item has no mfa input request, it was already provided | Nothing to do — the MFA was already submitted. |
| `ITEM_MFA_EXPIRED` | `400` | Item's MFA parameter expired, please start a new update | The MFA window closed. Start a new update to sync the connection. |
| `ITEM_MFA_PARAMETER_EXPECTED_MISMATCH` | `400` | Item is expecting ':parameter' MFA param name | The item is waiting for a different parameter. Use the name in the message. |
| `MFA_PARAMERTER_WAS_ALREADY_USED_ERROR` | `400` | MFA parameter has to be updated from last execution | The value sent is the one already used in the last execution. Ask the user for a new one. |
| `MISSING_MFA_PARAMETER_DATA` | `400` | Missing MFA parameter data | The request had no MFA parameters. Send the parameter the item is waiting for. |
| `MISSING_MFA_PARAMETER_VALUE` | `400` | Missing ':parameter' MFA parameter value | The parameter named in the message was sent empty. Send its value. |

<Callout variant="info" title="MFA_PARAMERTER_WAS_ALREADY_USED_ERROR">
That spelling is not a typo in this page: the API returns `PARAMERTER`. Match it
exactly if you branch on it.
</Callout>

## Real-time balance

Returned by [`GET /accounts/{id}/balance`](/reference/account-balance-get) — see [Real Time Balance](/docs/products/real-time-balance). Most of them relay what the financial institution answered.

| `codeDescription` | Status | Message | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `BALANCE_INVALID_REQUEST` | `400` | The balance request was rejected as invalid by the financial institution. | The institution rejected the request. Retrying the same request returns the same error; contact support with the `accountId` if it persists. |
| `BALANCE_CONSENT_ERROR` | `403` | The financial institution denied access to the account balance. The consent may be expired or missing the required permission. | The institution rejected the consent's access or denied access to the balance. The consent may be expired, revoked or missing the required permission; the user may need to reconnect the item. |
| `BALANCE_NOT_FOUND` | `404` | The account balance was not found at the financial institution. | The institution has no balance for this account. |
| `BALANCE_OPEN_FINANCE_RATE_LIMIT` | `429` | The financial institution rate-limited the balance request. Please try again later. | The institution's rate limit for this account was reached — for example its monthly balance quota, which is shared with item syncs. Retry later. |
| `BALANCE_FETCH_ERROR` | `500` | An error occurred while fetching the account balance from the connector | Retry later. |
| `BALANCE_CONNECTOR_UNAVAILABLE` | `502` | The financial institution is temporarily unavailable to provide the balance. Please try again later. | The institution is temporarily unavailable. Retry later. |
| `BALANCE_INSTITUTION_RATE_LIMITED` | `503` | The financial institution reached its global Open Finance request limit and is temporarily not answering. Please try again later. | The limit covers all the traffic the institution receives, not your application, so nothing is wrong with your request or the consent. Retry later with exponential backoff; no `Retry-After` header is sent. |

## Transactions

| `codeDescription` | Status | Message | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ENDPOINT_DEPRECATED` | `410` | This endpoint is deprecated. Use GET /v2/transactions with cursor pagination instead. | `GET /transactions` is closed for applications created on or after 2026-06-02 00:00 Brasília time (03:00 UTC), and available to everyone else only until 2026-12-31. Use [`GET /v2/transactions`](/reference/transaction/transactions-list-by-cursor) — see [the migration table](/reference/basic-concepts). |

Read the guide: [Errors Codes](/docs/developer-tools/error-codes).

## Rate Limits

Source: https://docs.pluggy.ai/en/docs/reference/rate-limits.md

Limits are counted **per endpoint, per IP, per minute** — not per account or per API key, so every server behind the same egress IP shares one budget. Each limit is independent: exhausting `POST /auth` does not affect `GET /transactions`. Where one limit spans two endpoints, requests to either count against it.

## Limits

| Endpoint | Requests per minute per IP |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /auth` | 360 |
| `GET /accounts`, `GET /accounts/{id}` | 360 |
| `GET /transactions`, `GET /transactions/{id}` | 360 |
| `GET /investments`, `GET /investments/{id}` | 360 |
| `GET /investments/{id}/transactions` | 360 |
| `GET /v2/items` | 360 |
| `GET /items/{id}/resources` | 360 |
| `GET /consents`, `GET /consents/{id}` | 360 |
| `PATCH /items/{id}` | 20 |

`PATCH /items/{id}` is sized for user-triggered updates. Daily refreshes belong to [auto-sync](/docs/connections/item#auto-sync), not to a loop of `PATCH` calls.

## The 429 response

```json
{
  "code": 429,
  "message": "Too many requests. Please try again later (see Retry-After header in seconds)"
}
```

Further requests to that endpoint keep failing until the minute window resets. Three headers say how long:

| Header | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `RateLimit-Limit` | The limit for this endpoint, per minute. |
| `RateLimit-Reset` | Seconds until the counter resets and the endpoint accepts requests again. |
| `Retry-After` | The standard retry hint. Always `60`. |

Wait `RateLimit-Reset` seconds and retry. HTTP clients with standard retry behaviour (for example `got`) already honour `Retry-After` on a `429`.

## Enrichment API

The Enrichment API (`enrichment-api.pluggy.ai`) has its own limit, counted differently: **600 requests per minute per application** (`clientId`), shared by `POST /categorize`, `POST /behavior-analysis` and `POST /recurring-payments`. Its `429` carries `Retry-After` (seconds until the window resets), `X-RateLimit-Limit` and `X-RateLimit-Remaining`. See [Transaction Enrichment](/docs/intelligence/transaction-enrichment#rate-limits).

## When you keep hitting a limit

- Reuse the API Key for its 2 hours instead of calling `POST /auth` per request — see [Authentication](/reference/authentication).
- Cap the parallelism of batch jobs against one endpoint and space the calls.
- Look for duplicated requests in normal operation.
- If the application genuinely needs more, contact support with the use case.

Read the guide: [Rate limits](/docs/developer-tools/rate-limits).

## Webhook

Source: https://docs.pluggy.ai/en/docs/reference/webhooks.md

A webhook is an HTTPS URL of yours that receives a `POST` with a JSON body when an event happens. Two ways to subscribe:

- **A Webhook resource** — [`POST /webhooks`](/reference/webhook/webhooks-create) with a `url` and an `event`. Delivers that event for every resource of the application.
- **`webhookUrl` on a resource** — set when creating an Item or a Connect Token. Delivers every event, but only for that resource (or the Items created with that token).

## Webhook resource

```http
POST https://api.pluggy.ai/webhooks
X-API-KEY: {apiKey}
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "url": "https://example.com/pluggy",
  "event": "item/updated",
  "headers": { "X-CLIENT-ID": "…" }
}
```

| Field | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | yes | A public HTTPS URL — see [URL requirements](#url-requirements). `localhost` is not accepted — use a tunnel such as ngrok while developing. |
| `event` | yes | One event from the tables below, or `all` for everything. There is no per-product wildcard: to receive every Item event, register `all` or one webhook per event. |
| `headers` | no | Sent with every delivery to this URL — the way to pass a secret your endpoint [verifies](/docs/developer-tools/webhooks-ref#verifying-notifications). Only configurable through the API, never shown in the dashboard. |

Endpoints: [`GET /webhooks`](/reference/webhook/webhooks-list), [`POST /webhooks`](/reference/webhook/webhooks-create), and retrieve, update and delete on [`/webhooks/{id}`](/reference/webhook).

### URL requirements

The `url` of a webhook — and the `webhookUrl` of an Item or a Connect Token — must be a public HTTPS endpoint:

| Rule | Rejected example |
| --- | --- |
| HTTPS only | `http://example.com/pluggy` |
| Default HTTPS port (443) only | `https://example.com:8443/pluggy` |
| No username or password in the URL | `https://user:pass@example.com/pluggy` |
| The host is a domain name, not an IP address | `https://203.0.113.10/pluggy` |
| No `localhost` or internal names (`.local`, `.internal`, `.localdomain`, `.home.arpa`) | `https://api.internal/pluggy` |
| The domain resolves only to public IP addresses | a domain that resolves to `10.0.0.5` |
| At most 2048 characters | — |

Tunnels and request-inspection services such as ngrok or webhook.site are accepted.

A URL that breaks a rule fails with `400`, and the message names the rule:

```json
{
  "code": 400,
  "message": "Webhook url must use the default https port"
}
```

<Callout variant="info">
Webhooks registered before a rule existed keep receiving events, but you can't update or re-enable one until its `url` follows every rule.
</Callout>

## Events

**Data**

| Event | Fires when |
| --- | --- |
| `item/created` | An Item was created and connected successfully. |
| `item/updated` | An Item was updated and synced successfully. |
| `item/deleted` | An Item was deleted. |
| `item/error` | An execution ended in error; `USER_AUTHORIZATION_PENDING` also fires this. |
| `item/waiting_user_input` | The Item needs input from the user (MFA) to continue. |
| `item/waiting_user_action` | The Item needs the user to act on their device — authorise in the bank app, scan a QR code. |
| `item/login_succeeded` | Login at the institution succeeded; data collection is running. |
| `connector/status_updated` | A connector changed status (`ONLINE`, `UNSTABLE`, `OFFLINE`). Carries `connectorId`. |
| `transactions/created` | New transactions after an update; carries `createdTransactionsLink` to fetch them. |
| `transactions/updated` | Transactions changed after an update; carries their ids. |
| `transactions/deleted` | Transactions removed after an update; carries their ids. |

Transaction events fire only when something changed; an update with no new transactions emits no `transactions/created`.

**Payments**

| Event | Fires when |
| --- | --- |
| `payment_intent/created` | A payment intent was created for a request. |
| `payment_intent/waiting_payer_authorization` | The intent needs the payer's authorisation. |
| `payment_intent/completed` | The intent completed. |
| `payment_intent/error` | The intent failed. |
| `payment_request/updated` | A payment request changed status. |
| `scheduled_payment/created`, `/completed`, `/error`, `/canceled` | One scheduled payment of an authorisation moved. |
| `scheduled_payment/all_created`, `/all_completed` | Every scheduled payment of an authorisation was created / completed. |
| `automatic_pix_payment/created`, `/completed`, `/error`, `/canceled` | A payment of an Automatic PIX request moved. |
| `smart_transfer_preauthorization/completed`, `/error` | A Smart Transfer pre-authorisation was approved, or failed. |
| `smart_transfer_payment/completed`, `/error` | A Smart Transfer payment settled, or failed. |

## Payload

Every notification carries:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `event` | The event name. |
| `eventId` | Identifies the event; the same value when one event is delivered to several URLs. |
| `clientId` | The Client ID of the application the webhook belongs to. Ignore a notification whose `clientId` isn't yours. |
| `triggeredBy` | `USER` (a Connect Token, e.g. the widget), `CLIENT` (an API Key, e.g. a `PATCH`), `SYNC` (auto-sync) or `INTERNAL` (Pluggy support). Absent on `item/deleted`, `connector/status_updated` and `transactions/deleted`. |
| the entity's id | `itemId` on Item events, `transactionIds` on transaction events, `connectorId` on connector events, and so on per event. |
| `clientUserId` | On `item/*` events only — the value set through the Connect Token's `options`. Not on `transactions/*`: map those to your user through `itemId`. |

```json
{
  "event": "item/updated",
  "eventId": "d876fd7c-e9bd-4c4c-bd46-cc96c62aac29",
  "clientId": "65a8c757-ef2c-4bc3-94ed-99218f6a0ee8",
  "itemId": "a5c763cb-0952-457b-9936-630f79c5b016",
  "triggeredBy": "SYNC",
  "clientUserId": "your-user-id"
}
```

## Delivery and retries

A delivery succeeds when your endpoint answers `2xx` **within 10 seconds**. Respond first, process afterwards — a slow handler is counted as a failure and retried.

On failure: **up to 3 attempts** in total — immediately, ~15 minutes after the first fails, then ~2 hours after the second. After that the event is discarded. Statuses `400`, `401`, `403`, `404` and `405` are never retried. Exception: `item/login_succeeded` and `item/waiting_user_input` get their 3 attempts ~6 minutes apart, never the 2-hour wait.

Redirects are not followed: a `3xx` counts as a failure. If the domain resolves to a private or reserved IP address when the notification is sent, it is not delivered and not retried.

When the application has a signing secret, every delivery carries `X-Pluggy-Signature` — see [Webhook security](/docs/developer-tools/webhook-security#4-verify-the-signature).

Read the guide: [Webhook](/docs/developer-tools/webhooks-ref) — payload examples per event, and troubleshooting.

## Server-Side SDKs

Source: https://docs.pluggy.ai/en/docs/reference/server-sdks.md

Three official server-side libraries wrap the API. Each is a thin client over the same endpoints in this reference; nothing is available in one that is not available over HTTP.

| Language | Package | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Node.js | `pluggy-sdk` (npm) | [pluggyai/pluggy-node](https://github.com/pluggyai/pluggy-node) |
| .NET | `Pluggy.SDK` (NuGet) | [pluggyai/pluggy-net](https://github.com/pluggyai/pluggy-net) |
| Java | `ai.pluggy:pluggy-java` (GitHub Packages) | [pluggyai/pluggy-java](https://github.com/pluggyai/pluggy-java) |

## Install

**Node.js**

```bash
npm install --save pluggy-sdk
```

**.NET**

```powershell
Install-Package Pluggy.SDK
```

**Java (Maven)**

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>ai.pluggy</groupId>
  <artifactId>pluggy-java</artifactId>
  <version>1.5.0</version>
</dependency>
```

The Java package is published to GitHub Packages, so `~/.m2/settings.xml` needs the GitHub Packages server with a personal access token — see [GitHub's Maven registry guide](https://docs.github.com/en/packages/working-with-a-github-packages-registry/working-with-the-apache-maven-registry).

## Generate your own

The OpenAPI 3 document that this reference renders is public:

```
https://api.pluggy.ai/oas3.json
```

Point a generator at it for any other language. Community clients exist too, for example [pluggy-python](https://github.com/diraol/pluggy-python); they are not maintained by Pluggy.

Read the guide: [Server-Side SDKs](/docs/developer-tools/server-sdks).

## Breaking changes and deprecations

**Pix Automático: the first payment cannot fall on the same day as the `startDate`.** Since 10/23, `POST /payments/requests/automatic-pix` returns `400 AUTOMATIC_PIX_INVALID_FIRST_PAYMENT_DATE` when the `firstPayment` date equals the `startDate`. If `firstPayment` has no `date`, it is settled on the day of authorization, and in that case the `startDate` cannot be today. The same validation runs on `POST /payments/intents`: requests already created in this format get the error there and must be recreated. This is an Open Finance rule: the recurrence only starts after the enrollment payment.

**What to do:** send a `startDate` at least one day after the first payment (for example, charge the enrollment today and start the monthly recurrence one month from now).

If you don't send `firstPayment`, you are not affected, and consents that are already authorized keep working.

---

**Client secret shown only once.** An application's client secret is now shown only at the moment it is generated: when the application is created or when you click "Generate new secret". After that, it can no longer be viewed in the Dashboard.

**What to do:** store the secret in a secure vault as soon as it is shown. If it is lost, generate a new one in the Dashboard.

Integrations that already use the secret keep working normally.

---

**Reminder — announced in June: transition to cursor pagination on the transactions endpoint.** Accounts created from June 2026 onward already use the cursor-paginated endpoint by default, and the legacy endpoint (v1) will be discontinued for those accounts in December 2026, one month from now.

**What to do:** migrate to the cursor-paginated endpoint. Accounts created before June 2026 remain unaffected, and we will give advance notice before any change for them.

</Callout>

## 💳 Payments

October brought PIX by biometrics, the first payment journey without a redirect to the bank, and reading the payer's account balance before charging.

- → **PIX by biometrics (Journey Without Redirect)** — You can now charge with PIX by biometrics. You create the request and send the `paymentUrl` to the payer. On the first payment, they choose the bank, approve the link and create a passkey at [pay.pluggy.ai](https://pay.pluggy.ai). On the following payments, on the same device, they confirm with biometrics, without being redirected to the bank's app. The API lets you create the charge, query the links and receive webhooks when a link is authorized, revoked or not completed. It is also available in the Node, Java and .NET SDKs and in the Dashboard, under **Payments → Requests** (new PIX by biometrics type) and **Payments → Linked accounts**. This is a first version, still without sandbox: to test it, use a real R$ 0.01 payment from an account different from the recipient's. For now the journey works only through Pluggy's payment page. Guides at [docs.pluggy.ai](https://docs.pluggy.ai), under Payments → PIX by biometrics.
- → **Source account balance with the Optimized Journey (Smart Transfers)** — When you create the preauthorization with `linkedJourney: true` in `POST /smart-transfers/preauthorizations`, the user authorizes, in the same approval at the bank, reading the source account balance. The preauthorization now includes `dataConsent` with the permission status (`AWAITING_AUTHORISATION`, `AUTHORISED` or `REJECTED`). With the permission authorized, `GET /smart-transfers/preauthorizations/{id}/balance` returns the real-time balance and the overdraft limit (`overdraft`). To revoke only this permission, use `DELETE /smart-transfers/preauthorizations/{id}/data-consent`: the preauthorization stays active. Each query goes to the institution and counts toward the Open Finance monthly quota, so query right before transferring. Applies only to new preauthorizations.
- → **Linked account balance in PIX by biometrics** — With `linkedJourney: true`, the payer can also share the balance and overdraft of the account they link, so you can check it before charging.

---

## 🚀 New Features

- → **Scheduled payments from checking accounts (Open Finance)** — Boletos, Pix and debits that the user has already scheduled at the bank now appear in `GET /transactions` as transactions with `status: PENDING` and `date` set to the scheduled date. When the payment is made, the transaction moves to `POSTED` keeping the same `id` (`transactions/updated` webhook). If the schedule is canceled, the transaction is removed (`transactions/deleted`). Scheduled payments do not affect the account `balance` until they are made. It starts with Itaú (601), up to 90 days ahead, and the next institutions will be added gradually. Note: if you query with `to` equal to today, you will not see scheduled payments. Use a `to` in the future.
- → **Richer real-time balance: `GET /accounts/{id}/balance`** — For Open Finance accounts, the endpoint now returns `blockedBalance`, `automaticallyInvestedBalance` and `closingBalance` (`balance` + `blockedBalance`). Optional fields are omitted when the institution does not provide them. The call also updates `bankData.closingBalance` and `bankData.automaticallyInvestedBalance` in `GET /accounts/{id}`, which previously only changed on the next sync. At Itaú and Banco do Brasil, `balance` already includes the automatic investment, so `balance` and `automaticallyInvestedBalance` carry the same value. Available in pluggy-node 0.93.0, pluggy-net 0.46.1 and pluggy-java 1.16.1.
- → **SCR in sandbox** — You can now test SCR without connecting a real account: create an item on the Sandbox Open Finance connector (600) with one of the sandbox CPFs and call `GET /items/{id}/scr`. The response is synthetic, deterministic and has the same format as production. It does not query Bacen and is not billed. The SCR feature still needs to be enabled for your team, and windows with more than 60 reference dates are rejected in sandbox.
- → **New tools in the Pluggy MCP** — From the assistant you already use (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor…), logged in with your Dashboard account, you can now investigate your integration without opening a ticket. `get_execution_reports` shows what each sync of an item brought: products with data, empty or failed, and transactions created, updated and removed. `summarize_api_calls` and `list_api_calls` show the calls your application made to the Pluggy API. `summarize_of_calls` and `list_of_calls` show the calls Pluggy made to the institution for each item, with the status of each one (for example, 429 for the bank's rate limit or 423 for the monthly limit). Each user only sees the applications and items of their own teams.

---

## 🖥️ Dashboard

- → **Request logs and metrics** — In the new **Monitor** section, the **Logs** page shows call, error and latency metrics for your application, with filters to find a request and the request and response detail for diagnosis. The section also brings together Webhooks and Analyze.
- → **API and Open Finance performance on the home page** — The Dashboard home separates the calls you make to the Pluggy API from the requests Pluggy sends to Open Finance institutions: volume, HTTP response distribution, most-called endpoints and p95 latency per endpoint. The Open Finance view covers the last 24 hours, per application.
- → **Execution explorer** — In Execution Troubleshooting, click an execution to see which products came with data, empty or failed, what the institution returned (accounts, cards, investments…) and the transactions created, updated and deleted. On the most recent execution, the panel also shows the item error and the state of each product. The history covers the item's last 20 executions.
- → **What's New** — The Dashboard now has a What's New area, with a quick introduction to each release and access to this changelog.
- → **Monitors (beta)** — On the new **Monitors** page, you set up alerts on your integration without depending on our team: create a monitor from templates with Pluggy's default values or define the metric, scope and condition, with a preview of the series and the threshold. When the monitor fires or recovers, the notice arrives by email or Slack, and active alerts and history are visible in the Dashboard. Monitors can be muted. Available on the Full and Full Plus plans; creating and editing monitors and channels requires the Owner or Admin role.

## 🐛 Fixes

- → **Future installments and pending card purchases (Itaú PF and C6, Open Finance)** — At Itaú PF (601), future installments are now dated within the bill they belong to and are no longer deleted before that bill closes. At C6 (626), recent pending purchases are no longer deleted and recreated when the bill closes. The fix applies to new purchases. Note: at Itaú PF, the `date` of a future installment is now the bill's date, not the purchase date.
- → **XP investments (Open Finance)** — New XP (602) investment positions stopped arriving when the institution's monthly query limit ran out, around mid-month. Positions now arrive on every update, without waiting for the month to turn.
- → **Investment fund taxes (Open Finance)** — Investment funds from Open Finance now include `taxes` (income tax provision) and `taxes2` (IOF provision), which previously came as `null`. This applies to all Open Finance institutions that report these values. Existing positions are corrected on the item's next sync.

## 🚀 New Features

- → **Resources declared in the consent: `GET /items/{id}/resources`** — A new endpoint lists the resources the institution declared for the item's consent, exactly as reported (`resourceId`, `type` and `status`). The `status` follows the Open Finance vocabulary: `AVAILABLE`, `UNAVAILABLE`, `TEMPORARILY_UNAVAILABLE` and `PENDING_AUTHORISATION`. An `UNAVAILABLE` or `PENDING_AUTHORISATION` resource explains a missing product. The Item's new `resourcesCollectedAt` field indicates whether the list has been read: if it is populated and the list is empty, the institution declared no resources; if it is `null`, the list has not yet been obtained. This applies only to Open Finance: items from direct connectors return an empty page without an error.
- → **Resources awaiting authorization: `hasResourcesPendingAuthorization`** — The Item now indicates whether the institution has resources awaiting authorization, a common case for business accounts that require a second approver. `true` means at least one resource is `PENDING_AUTHORISATION`, `false` means the list was read and nothing is pending, and `null` means the list has not been read or the connector is not Open Finance. To identify pending resources, use `GET /items/{id}/resources?status=PENDING_AUTHORISATION`. In `statusDetail`, pending investments and loans now generate `INV_002` and `LOAN_002` warnings. Already available in the Node (`pluggy-sdk` 0.91.0), Java (1.14.0) and .NET (0.43.0) SDKs.
- → **Product coverage per institution: `productCoverage`** — `GET /connectors` now reports which sub-products each Open Finance institution serves, using the Open Finance directory's names (for example, `CREDIT_OPERATIONS:LOANS`, `INVESTMENTS:FUNDS`, `INVESTMENTS:BANK_FIXED_INCOMES`). `products` tells you whether the institution serves investments; `productCoverage` tells you which ones. When the field is absent, coverage is unknown, as with direct connectors.
- → **Active incidents per connector: `health.incidents`** — `GET /connectors` and `GET /connectors/{id}` now include each connector's active incidents, with title, type, affected product, severity, state and status page link. The field appears only when there is an incident. Note that `health.status` may remain `ONLINE` while incidents are open. This lets you warn users on the bank selection screen before they try connecting to an institution experiencing issues.
- → **Status page API** — `status.pluggy.ai` now provides `GET /api/status`, with a complete snapshot (connector health, 90-day history and incidents with timelines), and `GET /api/summary`, with the overall status. No authentication is required. Each institution's identifier is the same `id` returned by `GET /connectors`.
- → **`operationType` on credit card transactions** — Open Finance credit card transactions now include the institution's transaction type in `operationType`, including `PAGAMENTO_FATURA`. Bill payment transactions that Pluggy generates from bills, which previously had `operationType: null`, now also use `PAGAMENTO_FATURA`. From now on, `operationType` may be supplied by the institution or inferred by Pluggy.
- → **New credit card transaction fields (Open Finance)** — `creditCardMetadata` now includes `paymentType` (`A_VISTA` or `A_PRAZO`), `billPostDate` (the date the institution posted the transaction to the bill, as reported) and `transactionDateTime` (transaction date and time, normalized to ISO-8601). `billPostDate` is `null` when the transaction has not yet been posted to a bill or the institution does not report the date. For transactions of type `OUTROS`, the institution's additional detail is now returned in `operationTypeAdditionalInfo`. The `date` field does not change. Fields are populated from subsequent updates, without retroactive changes: the key is absent on older transactions, and an absent key means the same as `null`.
- → **Taxes on equity investment transactions (Open Finance)** — Taxes reported by the institution on equity investment transactions are now returned in `expenses.other`. Withholding income tax (IRRF) remains in `incomeTax`.

## 💳 Payments

- → **Simulate synchronous failures in Pix Automático (sandbox)** — Use the amount R$ 404.04 in any Pix Automático request on the Sandbox Open Finance connector (first payment, authorization or recurring scheduling) to immediately receive `SANDBOX_FORCED_SYNC_ERROR`. Nothing is saved and no webhook is sent, simulating a bank that never responds. This lets you test a flow that differs from business errors such as insufficient funds.
- → **New Pluggy consent screen for simple Pix (sandbox)** — On the Pluggy Bank sandbox connector, simple Pix now has a Pluggy consent screen so you can test the payment flow end to end. The payment completes normally without getting stuck in `CONSENT_AWAITING_AUTHORIZATION`.
- → **Pix Automático: scheduling retry limit** — When creating a scheduled payment failed before the institution responded, the scheduler created another failed payment every few minutes without an error code. The failure now reports `AUTOMATIC_PIX_SCHEDULE_UNEXPECTED_ERROR`, and retries are limited per cycle. The fix applies to all production connectors.

## 🛠️ Resolved Incidents

- → **Bradesco Empresas (direct connector)** — The connector experienced recurring instability, including unavailability between September 4 and 6, and items ended in `PARTIAL_SUCCESS` because the payment data (`paymentData`) step failed on every execution. Both issues were fixed.

## 🐛 Fixes

- → **Pending credit card purchases are no longer deleted near bill closing** — On Itaú PF (601) and Nubank (612), pending purchases near the closing date were deleted and reappeared days later. On Open Finance connectors, an installment dated outside its bill could cause open purchases to be deleted. Both cases were fixed.
- → **Sicredi: pending approvals no longer cause connection errors** — On Sicredi PF (661) and Sicredi Empresas (627), consents for joint accounts or accounts with multiple approvers that were still awaiting approval returned `CONNECTION_ERROR`, as though the consent had been revoked. The item now stays in `USER_AUTHORIZATION_PENDING`, so you can guide the user to complete approval at the bank.
- → **Bradesco PJ (Open Finance): duplicate daily fee and charge entries** — Bradesco PJ (609) resends outstanding fee and charge entries every day with a new identifier, and each update saved another copy. New duplicates are no longer created.
- → **Installment amounts for credit card purchases (Open Finance)** — On Itaú, Banrisul and Inter, some installment purchases returned the total purchase amount for every installment instead of the installment amount. Each installment now carries its own amount.
- → **Itaú Empresas (direct connector): balances on AUT MAIS entries** — When AUT MAIS entry retrieval is enabled, automatic investments and withdrawals (`APL APLIC AUT MAIS` and `RES APLIC AUT MAIS`) now include `balance`, just like other statement entries.
- → **Credit card bills available from closing (Inter PF)** — On Inter PF (823), Open Finance credit card bills now arrive as soon as the institution publishes them at closing, rather than only on the due date. Other Open Finance connectors will receive this change progressively.

- → **SCR in the API reference** — `GET /items/{id}/scr` is now documented in the public reference, including response schemas, error codes and a new guide under Open Finance → SCR. The endpoint remains available to teams that have the feature enabled.

## Here are the main new features and improvements at Pluggy in August 2026.

August highlights

- **New minimum update frequency for new client IDs** — a small, protective breaking change, with higher frequencies available on request through Support.
- **New `GET /v2/items` endpoint** to list your connections with cursor pagination, available through a commercial agreement.

<Callout icon="⚠️" theme="warning">
## Breaking changes and deprecations

**Minimum update frequency now has a default for new client IDs.** Client IDs created from August onwards have a default value for `minUpdateFrequencyAllowedInHours`. Requesting an update before that interval returns `CLIENT_IS_UPDATING_BEFORE_ALLOWED_FREQUENCY`. This protects against overload without reducing product coverage.

**What to do:** if your integration needs more frequent updates, contact Support — the limit can be adjusted for each team on a case-by-case basis. **Existing client IDs are not affected.**

**`GET /transactions` (v1) now rejects more than 500 IDs in the `ids` parameter.** The request returns `400 IDS_PARAMETER_EXCEEDS_MAX_LENGTH`, matching the behavior already used by v2. Previously, v1 accepted the request without this validation.

**What to do:** split the query into batches of up to 500 IDs. If you consume `transactionIds` from the `transactions/updated` webhook, this is already handled — see the change under Webhooks.

---

**Reminder — announced in June: transition to cursor pagination on the transactions endpoint.** Accounts created from June 2026 onwards already use the cursor-paginated endpoint by default, and the legacy endpoint (v1) continues to be gradually discontinued for those accounts. This is the third notice, and the migration window remains open.

**What to do:** migrate to the cursor-paginated endpoint. Accounts created before June 2026 remain unaffected; we will give advance notice before any change for them.

**Reminder — announced in July: direct connectors for individuals are being discontinued.** Bradesco PF, Sicredi PJ and Itaú PF have already been delisted, and XP is following the same path. **The affected connections will be removed over the coming months**, and none have been removed yet.

**What to do:** migrate those connections to the equivalent Open Finance connector. There is no automatic migration — the end user must connect again, and the direct item's history is not transferred.
</Callout>

---

## 🚀 New Features

- → **List your connections: `GET /v2/items`** — Previously, it was not possible to list items through the API, so each integration had to store `itemId` values in its own database. The new endpoint returns your team's items from newest to oldest, with cursor pagination and the same fields as `GET /items/{id}`. It supports the `clientUserId` and `connectorId` filters. **It is opt-in:** disabled by default, it returns `403 LIST_ITEMS_FEATURE_NOT_ENABLED` until enabled. Listing can enumerate all of a team's items, which is broader access than fetching an item by ID, so activation requires a commercial agreement.
- → **Configurable update windows** — You can now configure the times when your items are updated automatically, instead of relying only on the default cycle. This is useful for detecting activity at specific times of day. Pluggy configures this on request — contact Support with the times that suit your integration.
- → **Open Finance Proxy available for high-volume connections** — Open Finance Proxy is no longer restricted to connections that have already reached an institution's resource limit (`RESOURCES_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`); it now also supports connections eligible based on volume. Pluggy determines eligibility and enables access per team after evaluation. **What to do:** if your connections have many accounts or a high volume of transactions and you encounter resource-limit failures, contact Support to assess enabling it for your team.

---

## 🔔 Webhooks

- → **`transactions/updated` is now sent in batches of up to 400 IDs** — For large updates, the webhook previously sent all `transactionIds` in one event, and the array did not fit in a single `GET /transactions?ids=` request. Now, 600 updated transactions generate two webhooks (400 + 200), each with its own `transactionsCount`. Each event fits in a single request and can be consumed directly without splitting the list.
- → **Fix for `PATCH /webhooks/{id}`** — The endpoint returned `500` when updating only the headers, even though the change was applied, and `400` saying the webhook already existed when `url` or `event` were provided, because the uniqueness validation compared the record against itself.

---

## 💳 Payments

- → **Clearer payment request error messages** — Messages returned when a payment request fails have been revised to explain more directly what happened and what to do.

---

## 🐛 Fixes

- → **Improvements to transaction deletion protection** — When an institution temporarily stopped returning existing transactions, they were marked as deleted and reappeared days later, causing gaps in statements and unintended deletion webhooks. Coordinated deletion is now suspended in these scenarios, preventing bank instability from causing data loss in your integration.
- → **Duplicate credit card bills when `billId` changes from provisional to final** — Before closing, the institution returns a provisional `billId` based on the projected due date, followed by the final ID after consolidation. If the due date changed during that transition, the two bills were not merged, resulting in a duplicate. The comparison now tolerates small date adjustments.
- → **Bradesco PJ (direct connector): missing transactions** — Fixed three cases that caused missing entries: period-based queries undercounted monthly volume and missed settled transactions during historical and partial syncs; identical entries repeated on the same day were discarded as duplicates; and a transaction that should appear three times was returned only once.
- → **Amount sign for recurring credit card payments** — In the Recurring Payments API (`POST /recurring-payments`), recurring credit card charges had a positive `averageAmount` and could be interpreted as income. The value now follows the banking convention stated in the documentation: expenses are negative. The same recurring payments continue to be detected — only the sign changes.
- → **Itaú Empresas (direct connector): investment sync restored** — Fixed the widespread failure that prevented investments from being returned since late July.
- → **Itaú: real-time AUT MAIS entries** — AUT MAIS entries are now available in real time, without the previous delay.

For individuals (PF) and businesses (PJ): 6P Bank, Apex, Axiis Bank, Banco BRB, BPO Bank, Ella Bank, Health Cash, Hiperbanco, Imobi Bank, Lothus, Meirelles, Nitybank, Ovni, PagueVeloz Serasa, Rapidium Bank, Resolve Bank, Rhiza Bank, Simpbank, Snob Bank, Uze and Won Bank. - **New endpoint to delete categorization rules** — `DELETE /categories/rules/:id` lets you delete a categorization rule created previously, completing the management cycle through the API.
- **Open Finance: automatic recovery of failed connections** — Open Finance connections that accumulate 5 consecutive errors are now reprocessed automatically once a day, until a successful sync recovers them. Previously, those connections stayed stuck and required a manual reconnection.

## 💳 Payments

- **Pix Automático: charge with cancelled consent fixed** — Fixed a case where a Pix Automático charge could be processed even after the consent had been cancelled.

- **Fixes in Payments** — Fixed the date shown for scheduled PIX, the creation of Pix Automático from the dashboard, and the recipient listing.

## 🐛 Fixes

- **Banco do Brasil: Rende Fácil balance** — Fixed a case where the balance showed as zero when the amount was invested in Rende Fácil. BB returns `availableAmount = 0` in that situation, and the invested amount is now taken into account in the account balance, as was already the case for Itaú.
- **Credit cards: bill dates and error isolation** — Fixed the closing and due dates when the institution returns bills out of chronological order, and fixed a case where a card with an error emptied the transactions of the other cards on the same item.
- **Investments** — Fixed the failure on Itaú PJ BBA accounts and improved the handling of rate limit errors in the investments connector.
- **More resilient syncs** — Avoided infinite runs on connections with `CONNECTION_ERROR`; fixed the dates used in partial syncs after a merge error; added a smart retry for first-time Sicoob connections that returned without data; fixed missing transactions on Sicoob (OF), on the BB PJ daily sync when `ACCOUNTS` was not among the products, and on Caixa PJ when the start date was earlier than the account opening.
- **Itaú: itemized SISPAG entries** — Fixed the handling of SISPAG salary entries that started being returned itemized after AUT MAIS was enabled.
- **Connectivity restored** — Stability restored on Nubank PF (Open Finance), XP and Celcoin.
- **Connect Widget: connect button** — Fixed cases where the connect button text did not appear or the button did not respond.
- **React Native SDK: OAuth connections on iOS** — `react-native-pluggy-connect@1.5.0` adds the `forceOauthInBrowser` prop. With `false`, OAuth opens in a WebView inside the app instead of the system browser, solving connections to regulated connectors that got stuck in `WAITING_USER_INPUT` until expiring on iOS. The default is still `true`, so the change is opt-in.

## 🚀 New Features

→ **Retry by time range** — resend webhooks from a specific period in case you missed an event.

→ **Retry from the dashboard** — resend webhooks directly from the interface, without having to use the API.

→ **Automatic deactivation of inactive URLs** — webhook URLs that have not received events for an extended period are automatically deactivated to avoid unnecessary calls.

→ **Webhook limit per event** — there is now a configurable limit of webhooks per event type for better organization.

***

## 🚀 New Features

→ **Account subtype (Open Finance)** — the `accountSubtype` field is now returned in the API response, providing more detail about the type of account connected.

→ **Filter by transaction creation date** — filter transactions by the date they were detected by Pluggy, useful for identifying new transactions since the last sync.

→ **Duplicate connection prevention** — during account selection with MFA, accounts that are already connected are blocked to avoid duplicates.

→ **CNPJ validation (Bradesco PJ)** — the CNPJ entered in the form is validated against the institution, avoiding connection errors.

***

## 🐛 Fixes

→ **Transaction dates** — fixed invalid dates on credit card transactions (Caixa) and boletos (Bradesco PJ).

→ **PDF statement (Itaú PJ)** — PDF statement download restored for Itaú PJ accounts.

→ **Itaú PJ connection** — resolved a connection error caused by permission expiration.

→ **Historical sync** — fixed an infinite loop that could occur during the sync of historical data via Open Finance.

→ **Duplicate transactions** — eliminated the duplication of transactions with the same identifier on the Banrisul and Banco do Brasil connectors.

→ **Webhook delivery** — fixed scenarios where transaction updated, item deletion and account creation webhooks were not delivered correctly (affected Inter MEI and Santander).

→ **Data fixes** — targeted adjustments to transactions on several connectors: Itaú, Bradesco, Santander, Banrisul, Banco do Brasil, Nubank, Sicredi, Caixa, BTG and Inter.

***

## 📚 Documentation

→ **Documentation for LLMs** — our documentation is now optimized for use with language models (AI), making AI-assisted integrations easier.

→ **Smart Transfers** — Smart Transfers documentation updated with the new capabilities.

→ **SDKs** updated to reflect the latest API features.

# :exclamation: New Product Alert

Batch Payment is available for all customers to review. You can dig into this feature in [this docs](https://docs.pluggy.ai/docs/bulk-payment-step-by-step).

<br />

Now you can pay multiple Pix, Boletos, and Taxes on a single transaction to multiple destinations using Pluggy's Smart Accounts.

Smart Accounts are accounts created for businesses to make easy transactions for them.\
This resource is also used for Transactional PIX through Pix QR, allowing customers to confirm the PIX reception as an alternative to PIS (Payment Initiation).

<br />

## ✨ Features ✨

* [OAS 3 ](https://api.pluggy.ai/oas3.json) of Pluggy's API it's publicly available for SDKs to be autogenerated.
* We have added Sicoob PF to our pool of Direct connections supporting all types of investments.
* Bank Cora PJ now supports login with account selection.
* XP supports redemption transfers for investments.
* Advisor connectors were created for XP Wealth & BTG Wealth, returning accounts, transactions, investments & investments transactions for all the advisor's customers.
* New connectors have been added for Open Finance Regulado, for the latest list review the [GET /connectors?isOpenFinance=true](https://docs.pluggy.ai/reference/connectors-list)
* Regulado connectors retrieving Fixed Incomes now are enhanced with Investment Data from Pluggy's sources.

<br />

## 🛠 Technical Additions

* Open Finance connector now syncs their health status with the Central Bank, providing webhooks of `connector/update` when they are unhealthy.

<br />

## :bug: Improvements

* Regulado connectors have received an improved performance boost on the first connections that collect the hole data of the user.
* Many more improvements!

## September 2023 (Monthly Update)

Source: https://docs.pluggy.ai/en/changelog#2023.09

### 🚀 **Open Finance Update: Bills, Investments & Identity Now Supported!**

#### Dive into the latest enhancements and additions we brought to you this month.

### ✨ **New Features** ✨

* 🌐 **Open Finance Flow Enhancements**:
  * Introduced [Investments](https://docs.pluggy.ai/docs/investments).
  * Rolled out [Bills](https://docs.pluggy.ai/docs/credit-card-bills).
  * Launched support for [Loans](https://docs.pluggy.ai/docs/loans) 
  * Implement [Identity](https://docs.pluggy.ai/docs/identities) product.
* 🏦 **Connectors**:
  * Enabled Mutual Funds and Fixed Income Investment Transactions for **Bradesco PJ** and **Banco do Brasil PJ**.
  * Sold Investments are now marked as `TOTAL_WITHRAWAL` in **Itau PF** and **Inter PF**.
  * Added Multiple Accounts support in **Ailos PF**.
  * Welcomed **EQI** as our new Connector. Discover its range of supported products [here](https://docs.pluggy.ai/docs/connectors-coverage#investment).
  * Added support for investment transactions in **Inter PF** 
  * Add account selection flow in the **XP Connector**.
* 🛠 **Technical Additions**:
  * Enhanced our connector model with `isSandbox` and `isOpenFinance` flags.
  * Added pagination for [Investments response](https://docs.pluggy.ai/reference/investments-list) using `page` and `pageSize` query parameters.

### 🛠 **Bug Fixes** 🛠

* Rectified Pix QR payment data anomalies in **Bradesco PJ**.

## May 2023 (Monthly Update)

* We have improved the **Bradesco PF** credit cards response fixing bill dates for installments.

* We have improved the credit card transactions with installments recalculating the date in **Santander PF**.
* We have improved the transactions response in **Santander PJ** supporting the `Provider Code`.
* We have improved credit cards response in **Banco do Brasil PF** by adding **balanceCloseDate**.
* We improved our Deel connector, providing a single access for Contractors & Businesses, to collect their financial data. Providing the Business with their employee's contracts & their payments.

## March 2023 (Monthly Update)

Source: https://docs.pluggy.ai/en/changelog#2023.03

We are ending our Q1 with this news!!

:sparkles:  Features

* We added `eventId` on our [webhooks payload](https://docs.pluggy.ai/docs/webhooks#payload-parameters). This field identifies the event itself univocally allowing our clients to be sure if the event is already processed.

* As part of our **Q1-2023 Hackathon**, we have shipped a lot of connectors that are in BETA and ready to get feedback for our users:
  * Lemon Cash (Retail Bank)
  * Iti (Retail Bank)
  * Wise (Retail Bank)
  * Warren Investimentos (Broker)
  * Deel  (Contractors & Business - Digital Economy)
  * OnTop (Digital Economy)
  * Stone (PSP)
  * Splitwise (Personal Finance Management).
  * MeuVivo (Telecommunication)
  * ContaAzul (Invoicing)

* We are launching our [MeuPluggy](https://meu.pluggy.ai) consent management platform where all the users that shared their access through our platform can manage their consents, review their data and revoke any access that they want to restrict. **This is automatically provided for all our customers.**

* [OAuth v2](https://docs.pluggy.ai/docs/connect-an-account#oauth-v2) has been launched at Pluggy, for some new connectors provided in the news above. This new flow allows tracking the user's connection through the complete flow.

* We added `consecutiveFailedLoginAttempts` to our item entity in order to warn users when they’re about to cause ACCOUNT\_LOCKED on their own accounts.

* We launch [INCOME REPORTS](https://docs.pluggy.ai/docs/income-report-beta) new product for XP connector!!

* We have added the "Item's Execution" overview page to our dashboard, you can now go deeper into the item's health by analyzing the item by its ID.

* ![](https://files.readme.io/c730da7-image.png)

:heart_decoration: Improvements

* We have improved our [Categorization documentation](https://docs.pluggy.ai/docs/transaction-categories), providing more insights about this feature, and what else can be achieved from this.

:dizzy_face: Sad news

* To improve scalability and performance with Investment transactions, we are not deprecating the `transactions` field in `GET /investments` and `GET /investments/{id}` in favor of our paginated [Investment Transactions](https://docs.pluggy.ai/reference/investment-transactions-list) endpoint. We will no longer return the \`transactions´ field in Investments for new Applications, created from 21st March 2023 onward.

## February 2023 (Monthly Update)

Source: https://docs.pluggy.ai/en/changelog#2023.02

Happy Carnaval from Pluggy! :tada:\
This month we did a little more than enjoy the holidays, and here is just the summary of it.

:sparkles:  Features

* We have added the `ACCOUNT_CREDENTIALS_RESET` execution error for users that face this situation forced by the financial institution to refresh due to expired credentials or new measures taken by the institution. No synchronization will happen until the item is updated with the new set of credentials. 

* We are returning the `metadata` response for **Nuinvest**, **BTG Pactual** & **Orama** allowing Previdencia Portability for the financial institution. 

* We added the `investorProfile` field to our `identity` product, which indicates the investor's personality and motivation for investing. This is already being recovered on **XP Investimentos** & **BTG Pactual**, adding it to more institutions for the next month.

* **XP Investimentos** & **Ailos** now supports the product **Credit Card** and it's **Transactions**, returning up to 12 months of historic data.

:heart_decoration: Improvements

* We have improved **Genial Investimentos** investment transaction's response with Taxes, Transfers & Sales operations. 

* Warnings now have more details about the `code` related to the warning and, if provided, will return the `providerMessage` a user-friendly message directly from the financial institution. 

From recent updates, all SDKs have been updated and are kept updated to the latest changes that our API occurs. Please visit the specific SDK public GitHub repository for more information.

:dizzy_face: Sad news

* We have deprecated our **C6 Connector** due to security restrictions from the financial institution. For the time being it won't be available, until something change in the future. All existing connections can still be recovered from our API.

<!-- pluggy-readme-source:february-2023-monthly-update -->

* We have delivered and it's in **BETA** the **Avenue Broker Connector**!\
  You can now recover your checking account, transactions and investments (mutual funds, equities & ETFs).\
  This is already available in our [dashboard](https://dashboard.pluggy.ai) for you to enable on your application.\
  Feel free to reach out with any problems or doubts.

* **Genial Broker** keeps growing support for asset transactions, now we are returning transactions for assets of type Securities, Fixed Income & Equities.

* Pss it's coming home! **Portfolio Yield** is on public **BETA**. Providing a historic & whole view of your user's portfolio performance month over month. We are preparing the beta launch for *XP Investimentos* accounts.\
  Reach out to [support@pluggy.ai](mailto:support@pluggy.ai) or chat with us, if you want to join the BETA!

* Did you know the [Opportunities](https://docs.pluggy.ai/docs/opportunity) product? It provides a great vision of what products are the financial institutions offering to your users. This provides a competitive battleground to deliver improved products to your users. Now available on the **Itau Business** connector as well!

* We have improved the `health` object that now provides **statistics about your recent connections on the connector and recent connection rate** (percentage of healthy connections) that can be recovered when listing the connectors, check it out under the [API Reference](https://docs.pluggy.ai/reference/connectors-list). 

```json Connector's list response
{
  "page": 1,
  "total": 1,
  "totalPages": 1,
  "results": [
    {
      "id": 201,
      "name": "Itaú",
      "type": "PERSONAL_BANK",
      "credentials": [],
      "products": [],
      "health": {
        "status": "ONLINE",
        "stage": null,
        "details": {
            "connectionRateLast6Hours": 94.3,
            "connectionsLast6Hours": 53
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

:heart_decoration: Improvements

* We have sped up the process of recovering customized Terms & Conditions.\
  Did you know that terms & conditions can be customized?

* Major improvement on **XP Investimentos**! After a significant blocker, and some weeks of instability, we launched the v2 of the connector improving the performance of the connection by more than 50%.\
  Due to the blocker, we are not returning Equities & Securities transactions.

* **Banco do Brasil** it's returning future transactions as `PENDING` now available for all Credit Cards & Accounts.

* When a Connector requires [an MFA Token to execute an update](https://docs.pluggy.ai/reference/items-update) (ie. Bradesco PF), the API will require this input to be different from the previous one. If not, it will return an HTTP 400 error.

```json HTTP 400 error
{
  "code": 400,
  "message": "MFA parameter has to be updated from last execution"
}
```

* We have increased the "Sandbox" coverage for all the different flows available (yep, there are too many!!). It's important for you to test each one of those.
  * Sandbox connectors can be found with `connectorId` lower than 99.
  * If you are using the *Pluggy Connect* widget, you will have the following experience.

![400](https://files.readme.io/b18b41c-Fintouch.png "Fintouch.png")

:ballot_box_with_check: Fixed

* Fixed `clientUserId` not being propagated to item connections for **MercadoPago** connector. This only affected *Pluggy Connect* connections.

## Remember, we are one text message away!

For any doubt, issues, or BETA access, please reach out through our chat. We will get back to you as soon as possible.\
Also, you can check out our latest Dashboard features that will improve your day-to-day. 

![400](https://files.readme.io/5515618-Intercom.png "Intercom.png")
